lessons.u: Module 4: Angle measure and plane figures
lessons.n: Classifying two-dimensional figures and lines of symmetry

it.q: A triangle has one angle that measures exactly 90 degrees. What kind of triangle is it?
it.h: Which kind of triangle is named for a 90-degree angle?

it.q: A triangle has three sides that are each 5 cm long. Which name fits?
it.h: "Equi" means equal.

it.q: How many lines of symmetry does a square have?
it.h: Count every fold that makes the two halves match, including the diagonals.

it.q: Which quadrilateral always has two pairs of parallel sides and four right angles?
it.h: Which shape must have square corners?

it.q: How many lines of symmetry does a rectangle that is not a square have?
it.h: Try folding across the middle each way, then try the diagonals.

it.q: Which triangle has no sides of equal length?
it.h: Isosceles triangles have at least two equal sides.

it.q: Explain how you can test whether a line is a line of symmetry.
it.ans: Fold the figure along the line. If the two halves match exactly, the line is a line of symmetry.

lessons.u: Module 4: Angle measure and plane figures
lessons.n: Classifying triangles by angles and sides

it.q: A triangle has one 90-degree angle. What kind of triangle is it?
it.h: A 90-degree angle is a right angle.

it.q: A triangle has angles of 40, 60 and 80 degrees. What kind of triangle is it?
it.h: Are all three angles less than 90 degrees?

it.q: A triangle has angles of 30, 40 and 110 degrees. What kind of triangle is it?
it.h: Is one angle greater than 90 degrees?

it.q: A triangle has angles of 90, 50 and 40 degrees. How many of its angles are acute?
it.h: An acute angle is less than 90 degrees.

it.q: Can a triangle have two right angles?
ch: no, the other two sides would be parallel and never meet
it.h: Draw a side with a right angle at each end. Do the other two sides ever meet?

it.q: Draw an acute triangle and an obtuse triangle. Explain how they are different.
it.ans: All angles of the acute triangle are less than 90 degrees. The obtuse triangle has one angle greater than 90 degrees.

lessons.u: Module 4: Angle measure and plane figures
lessons.n: Multi-step unknown angle problems

it.q: Three angles meet at a point on a straight line. Two are 45 and 70 degrees. How many degrees is the third angle?
it.h: Angles on a straight line add to 180 degrees.

it.q: A right angle is split into three angles. Two are 25 and 30 degrees. How many degrees is the third?
it.h: A right angle is 90 degrees.

it.q: Four angles go all the way around a point. Three are 90, 100 and 80 degrees. Which equation finds the fourth angle, x?
it.h: A full turn is 360 degrees.

it.q: Four angles go all the way around a point. Three are 90, 100 and 80 degrees. How many degrees is the fourth?
A straight angle is split into two angles. One is 3 times as large as 40 degrees. How many degrees is the other angle?
it.h: 3 x 40 = 120. The two angles add to 180.

it.q: Two angles together make a right angle. One angle is 2 times the other. Find both angles and explain.
it.ans: The angles are 30 and 60 degrees, because 30 + 60 = 90 and 60 is 2 times 30.

lessons.u: Module 5: Fraction equivalence, ordering and operations
lessons.n: Decomposing fractions and finding equivalent fractions

it.q: Which shows 3/5 decomposed into unit fractions?
it.h: A unit fraction has a numerator of 1.

it.q: 2/3 = ?/12. What is the missing numerator?
it.h: What do you multiply 3 by to get 12? Multiply the numerator by the same number.

it.q: Which fraction is equivalent to 9/12?
it.h: Divide the numerator and the denominator by the same number.

it.q: 5/10 = 1/?. What is the missing denominator?
it.h: What number do you divide 5 by to get 1?

it.q: Which is NOT a way to decompose 5/8?
it.h: Add each set of parts. Which one does not make 5/8?

it.q: Use an area model to explain why 1/4 = 3/12.
it.ans: Draw a rectangle cut into 4 equal parts and shade 1 part. Cut each part into 3 equal pieces. Now there are 12 pieces and 3 are shaded, but the shaded amount did not change, so 1/4 = 3/12.

lessons.u: Module 5: Fraction equivalence, ordering and operations
lessons.n: Comparing fractions

it.q: Which symbol makes 3/8 __ 1/2 true?
it.h: 1/2 is the same as 4/8.

it.q: Which fraction is greater than 1/2?
it.h: Compare each numerator with half of its denominator.

it.q: Which comparison is true?
it.h: Rename both fractions with a denominator of 15.

it.q: Kiran ran 5/6 mile and Ali ran 7/12 mile. How much farther did Kiran run, in miles?
it.h: Rename 5/6 as twelfths first.

it.q: Order from least to greatest: 3/4, 5/8, 7/12
it.h: Rename all three fractions with a denominator of 24.

it.q: Explain how to use 1/2 as a benchmark to compare 3/7 and 5/9.
it.ans: 3/7 is less than 1/2 because 3 is less than half of 7. 5/9 is more than 1/2 because 5 is more than half of 9. So 3/7 < 5/9.

lessons.u: Module 5: Fraction equivalence, ordering and operations
lessons.n: Adding and subtracting fractions with like denominators

it.h: Add the number of sevenths. The size of the pieces does not change.
Subtract the number of tenths.
1 whole is 8/8.

it.q: Which sum is equal to 5/6?
it.h: Add the sixths in each choice.

it.q: A pitcher has 7/8 liter of juice. Sam pours 3/8 liter into one glass and 2/8 liter into another. How many liters are left in the pitcher?
it.h: Add the amounts poured first, or subtract one amount at a time.

it.q: Explain why 3/5 + 1/5 is 4/5 and not 4/10.
it.ans: The pieces are fifths. 3 fifths plus 1 fifth is 4 fifths. The denominator names the size of the pieces, and that size does not change when you add.

lessons.u: Module 5: Fraction equivalence, ordering and operations
lessons.n: Mixed numbers: renaming, adding and subtracting

it.q: Which is 11/4 written as a mixed number?
it.h: How many groups of 4/4 are in 11/4? How many fourths are left?

it.q: Write 3 2/5 as a fraction greater than 1.
it.h: Each whole is 5/5. How many fifths are in 3 wholes?
Add the wholes, then add the eighths.
There are not enough sixths to subtract. Rename 1 whole as 6/6.

it.q: Which equals 5 1/3 - 2 2/3?
it.h: Rename 5 1/3 as 4 4/3 first.

it.q: Explain two ways to solve 3 3/4 + 1 2/4.
it.ans: Add wholes and parts: 4 + 5/4 = 4 + 1 1/4 = 5 1/4. Or change both to fractions: 15/4 + 6/4 = 21/4 = 5 1/4.

lessons.u: Module 5: Fraction equivalence, ordering and operations
lessons.n: Multiplying a fraction by a whole number and fraction line plots

it.h: Think of 4 groups of 1 fifth.
3 groups of 2 sevenths is how many sevenths?
5 groups of 3 fourths is 15 fourths.

it.q: Which is equal to 3/8 + 3/8 + 3/8 + 3/8?
it.h: How many groups of 3/8 are added?

it.q: A recipe uses 2/3 cup of oats for one batch. How many cups of oats are needed for 6 batches?
it.h: Find 6 x 2/3, then rename the answer as a whole number.

it.q: Use a number line to explain why 6 x 2/5 = 12/5.
it.ans: Make 6 jumps of 2/5 from 0: 2/5, 4/5, 6/5, 8/5, 10/5, 12/5. Six groups of 2 fifths is 12 fifths, which is 2 2/5.

lessons.u: Module 5: Fraction equivalence, ordering and operations
lessons.n: Fraction word problems with like denominators

it.q: Ana ran 3/8 mile in the morning and 4/8 mile after school. What is the numerator of the fraction of a mile she ran in all, in eighths?
it.h: Add the numerators. The denominator stays 8.

it.q: A ribbon is 9/10 meter long. Tom cuts off 4/10 meter. How long is the ribbon now?
it.h: Subtract the numerators.

it.q: A pizza is cut into 6 equal slices. Kim eats 2/6 and Lu eats 3/6. What fraction is left?
it.h: First add what they ate. The whole is 6/6.

it.q: A recipe uses 2 1/4 cups of flour and 1 3/4 cups of sugar. How many cups is that in all?
it.h: Add the wholes, then add the fourths.

it.q: Jay walked 1 2/5 miles. Mai walked 3/5 mile less. How far did Mai walk?
it.h: Rename 1 2/5 as 7/5.

it.q: A jug has 2 1/3 liters of juice. The class drinks 1 2/3 liters. How much is left? Show your work.
it.ans: Rename 2 1/3 as 7/3 and 1 2/3 as 5/3. 7/3 - 5/3 = 2/3 liter.

lessons.u: Module 5: Fraction equivalence, ordering and operations
lessons.n: Multiplying a fraction by a whole number in word problems

it.q: Each student needs 2/3 cup of clay. How many cups do 6 students need?
A runner runs 3/4 mile each day for 5 days. How far does she run?
it.h: Multiply the numerator by 5.

it.q: A recipe uses 3/8 cup of oil. Ben makes 4 batches. How many eighths of a cup does he use?
it.h: 4 x 3 = 12 eighths.

it.q: Which is equal to 7 x 1/5?
it.h: 7 groups of 1 fifth.

it.q: A snail crawls 5/6 meter each hour. How many meters does it crawl in 6 hours?
Each of 3 friends eats 3/4 of a sandwich. Is that more or less than 2 whole sandwiches? Explain.
it.ans: 3 x 3/4 = 9/4 = 2 1/4 sandwiches, which is more than 2.

lessons.u: Module 6: Decimal fractions
lessons.n: Tenths as fractions and decimals

it.q: Which decimal equals 3/10?
it.h: The first place to the right of the decimal point is the tenths place.

it.q: Write 7/10 as a decimal.
it.h: How many tenths are there?

it.q: A meter stick is marked in 10 equal parts. A ribbon starts at 0 and reaches the 6th mark. How long is the ribbon?
it.h: Each part is 1 tenth of a meter.

it.q: Write 2 4/10 as a decimal.
it.h: The whole number goes to the left of the decimal point.

it.q: Where is 1.5 on a number line?
it.h: 1.5 is 1 whole and 5 tenths.

it.q: Explain why 0.8 and 8/10 name the same number.
it.ans: 0.8 means 8 tenths, because the 8 is in the tenths place. 8/10 also means 8 tenths, so they are the same number.

lessons.u: Module 6: Decimal fractions
lessons.n: Hundredths and equivalent decimals

it.q: Which decimal equals 45/100?
it.h: The second place to the right of the decimal point is the hundredths place.

it.q: 3/10 = ?/100. What is the missing numerator?
it.h: Each tenth is 10 hundredths.

it.q: Write 6/100 as a decimal.
it.h: 6 hundredths has no tenths. What digit goes in the tenths place?

it.q: Which decimal is equal to 0.7?
it.h: 7 tenths is how many hundredths?

it.q: 4/10 + 25/100 = ? Write the answer as a fraction with a denominator of 100.
it.h: Rename 4/10 as hundredths first.

it.q: Explain why 0.50 has the same value as 0.5.
it.ans: 0.5 is 5 tenths. Each tenth is 10 hundredths, so 5 tenths = 50 hundredths = 0.50. The zero in the hundredths place adds no value.

lessons.u: Module 6: Decimal fractions
lessons.n: Comparing decimals

it.q: Which symbol makes 0.6 __ 0.45 true?
it.h: Rename 0.6 as hundredths.

it.q: Which decimal is greatest?
it.h: Compare the tenths digits first.

it.q: Order from least to greatest: 0.3, 0.27, 0.32
it.h: Write each decimal as hundredths: 30, 27 and 32 hundredths.

it.q: Which is greater, 1.4 or 1.38? Write the greater number.
it.h: Both have 1 whole. Compare the tenths.

it.q: One snail crawled 0.5 m and another crawled 0.48 m. Which statement is true?
ch: The first snail crawled 2 hundredths of a meter farther
The first snail crawled 43 hundredths of a meter farther
it.h: Write both distances as hundredths of a meter.

it.q: Explain how a meter stick can show that 0.7 m is longer than 0.65 m.
it.ans: 0.7 m is 70 cm and 0.65 m is 65 cm. On a meter stick, 70 cm is farther from 0 than 65 cm, so 0.7 m is longer.

lessons.u: Module 6: Decimal fractions
lessons.n: Adding tenths and hundredths and money amounts

it.q: 3/10 + 45/100 = ? Write the answer as a decimal.
it.h: Rename 3/10 as 30/100.

it.q: Write 65 cents as a decimal number of dollars.
it.h: A dollar is 100 cents, so 1 cent is 1 hundredth of a dollar.

it.q: What is the value of 3 quarters and 2 dimes, in dollars?
it.h: A quarter is 25 cents and a dime is 10 cents.

it.q: 2 3/10 + 1 46/100 = ? Write the answer as a decimal.
it.h: Add the wholes, then rename the tenths as hundredths and add.

it.q: Kim has 2 one-dollar bills, 3 dimes and 4 pennies. How many dollars does she have, written as a decimal?
it.h: Find the cents first: 3 dimes and 4 pennies.

it.q: Explain why 6/10 + 7/100 is not 13/110.
it.ans: You cannot add the denominators. Rename 6/10 as 60/100, then 60/100 + 7/100 = 67/100, or 0.67.

lessons.u: Module 6: Decimal fractions
lessons.n: Decimals on the number line and in money

it.q: A number line from 0 to 1 has 10 equal parts. What decimal is at the 7th mark?
it.h: Each mark is one tenth.

it.q: Which decimal is halfway between 2.3 and 2.5?
it.h: Count by tenths from 2.3.

it.q: How many cents is $0.35?
it.h: One cent is one hundredth of a dollar.

it.q: Which decimal names 4 dollars and 8 cents?
it.h: 8 cents is 8 hundredths of a dollar.

it.q: A number line from 1 to 2 is marked in hundredths. Point P is 36 marks past 1. What decimal is P?
it.h: Each mark is 0.01.

it.q: Explain why 0.5 and 0.50 are at the same point on a number line.
it.ans: 0.5 is 5 tenths and 0.50 is 50 hundredths. 5 tenths equal 50 hundredths, so they are the same point.

lessons.u: Module 6: Decimal fractions
lessons.n: Decimal measurement word problems

it.q: A plant was 0.4 meter tall. It grew 0.35 meter. How tall is it now in meters?
it.h: Change 0.4 to 0.40, then add hundredths.

it.q: Kai has $3.60. He buys a snack for $1.25. How much money does he have left in dollars?
it.h: Subtract dollars and cents, or count up from $1.25.

it.q: A ribbon is 0.8 meter long. Which length is longer?
it.h: Compare tenths, then hundredths.

it.q: Ming ran 1.5 km on Monday and 2.25 km on Tuesday. How many kilometers did she run?
it.h: Write 1.5 as 1.50.

it.q: A book costs $4.75 and a pen costs $0.80. What is the total?
it.h: Add the cents: 75 + 80 = 155 cents.

it.q: Explain how to add 0.6 liter and 0.27 liter using fractions.

lessons.u: Module 7: Exploring measurement with multiplication
lessons.n: Customary length and conversion tables

it.q: How many inches are in 1 foot?
it.h: Look at a 12-inch ruler.

it.q: How many feet are in 1 yard?
it.h: Think about a yardstick and a 1-foot ruler.

it.q: How many inches are in 5 feet?
it.h: Each foot is 12 inches.

it.q: A table shows 1 ft = 12 in, 2 ft = 24 in and 3 ft = 36 in. Which rule changes feet to inches?
it.h: What do you do to 1, 2 and 3 to get 12, 24 and 36?

it.q: How many inches are in 4 feet 7 inches?
it.h: Convert the feet to inches, then add the extra inches.

it.q: Explain why the number of inches is always 12 times the number of feet for the same length.
it.ans: Each foot is made of 12 inches. If a length is some number of feet, it is that many groups of 12 inches.

lessons.u: Module 7: Exploring measurement with multiplication
lessons.n: Converting weight, liquid volume and time

it.q: How many ounces are in 1 pound?
it.h: A pound is a larger unit made of 16 smaller units.

it.q: How many cups are in 1 quart?
it.h: 1 quart = 2 pints and 1 pint = 2 cups.

it.q: How many ounces are in 3 pounds?
it.h: Multiply the pounds by 16.

it.q: How many minutes are in 4 hours?
it.h: Each hour is 60 minutes.

it.q: Which is equal to 2 gallons?
it.h: 1 gallon = 4 quarts.

it.q: Make a table for 1, 2, 3 and 4 gallons in quarts and explain the pattern.
it.ans: 1 gallon = 4 quarts, 2 = 8, 3 = 12 and 4 = 16 quarts. Each gallon adds 4 quarts, so the quarts are always 4 times the gallons.

lessons.u: Module 7: Exploring measurement with multiplication
lessons.n: Measurement word problems with mixed units

it.q: Ari's puppy weighed 4 pounds 10 ounces. It gained 2 pounds 9 ounces. How many ounces does it weigh now?
it.h: Convert both weights to ounces, or add pounds and ounces separately and regroup.

it.q: A board is 8 feet long. Two pieces that are each 2 feet 9 inches long are cut from it. How many inches of the board are left?
it.h: Change all the lengths to inches first.

it.q: 3 hours 40 minutes + 1 hour 35 minutes = ?
it.h: 40 + 35 minutes is more than 60 minutes. Make a new hour.

it.q: Ms. Ray buys 3 gallons of juice. She serves 30 cups. How many cups of juice are left?
it.h: Change the gallons to cups. 1 gallon = 16 cups.

it.q: A runner trains for 45 minutes each day for 6 days. How many minutes does she train in all?
it.h: Multiply the minutes for one day by the number of days.

it.q: Explain two ways to solve 5 feet 3 inches - 2 feet 8 inches.
it.ans: Convert to inches: 63 - 32 = 31 inches, which is 2 feet 7 inches. Or rename 1 foot as 12 inches: 4 feet 15 inches - 2 feet 8 inches = 2 feet 7 inches.

lessons.u: Module 7: Exploring measurement with multiplication
lessons.n: Measurements as fractions and mixed numbers

it.q: What fraction of a foot is 6 inches?
it.h: A foot has 12 inches. What part of 12 is 6?

it.q: How many inches are in 2 1/2 feet?
it.h: Half of a foot is 6 inches.

it.q: How many ounces are in 1/4 pound?
it.h: Split 16 ounces into 4 equal parts.

it.q: How many minutes are in 3/4 hour?
it.h: Find 1/4 of 60 minutes first.

it.q: Which is equal to 1 1/2 gallons?
it.h: 1 gallon is 4 quarts. What is half of a gallon?

it.q: One loaf of bread uses 3/4 cup of milk. How many cups of milk are needed for 8 loaves?
it.h: Multiply 8 x 3/4 and rename the answer.

it.q: Explain why 1/3 yard is the same length as 1 foot.
it.ans: A yard is 3 feet. Splitting a yard into 3 equal parts makes each part 1 foot, so 1/3 yard = 1 foot.

lessons.u: Module 7: Exploring measurement with multiplication
lessons.n: Elapsed time and time conversions in word problems

it.q: A movie is 2 hours 15 minutes long. How many minutes is that?
it.h: 1 hour is 60 minutes.

it.q: A train ride starts at 9:45 a.m. and ends at 1:20 p.m. How many minutes long is the ride?
it.h: 9:45 to 12:45 is 3 hours. 12:45 to 1:20 is 35 minutes.

it.q: Which is longer, 3 hours or 175 minutes?
it.h: 3 hours is 180 minutes.

it.q: Practice is 45 minutes a day for 6 days. How many hours is that in all? Write the answer as a mixed number.
it.h: 45 x 6 = 270 minutes. How many 60s are in 270?

it.q: A race took 3 minutes 25 seconds. How many seconds is that?
it.h: 1 minute is 60 seconds.

it.q: A baker starts at 5:40 a.m. and works 7 hours 35 minutes. When does she finish? Explain.

lessons.u: Module 7: Exploring measurement with multiplication
lessons.n: Area and perimeter formulas in real-world problems

it.q: A rectangular room is 14 feet long and 12 feet wide. What is its area in square feet?
it.h: Area = length x width.

it.q: A garden is 23 meters long and 9 meters wide. How many meters of fence go around it?
it.h: Perimeter = 2 x length + 2 x width.

it.q: A rug has an area of 96 square feet and a length of 12 feet. What is its width in feet?
A rectangle has a perimeter of 50 cm and a length of 15 cm. What is its width?
it.h: Two lengths are 30 cm. Split what is left between two widths.

it.q: Carpet costs $6 per square foot. A room is 10 feet by 13 feet. How many dollars does carpet cost?
it.h: Find the area first.

it.q: A farmer has 36 meters of fence for a rectangular pen. Find two possible sizes and their areas. Which gives more space?
it.ans: Examples: 10 m by 8 m has area 80 square meters; 12 m by 6 m has area 72. The 10 by 8 pen gives more space (a 9 by 9 square gives the most, 81).

lessons.u: Module 1: Place value and decimal fractions
lessons.n: Multiplying and dividing by powers of ten

it.h: When you multiply by 10, each digit moves one place to the left.
Dividing by 100 moves each digit two places to the right.

it.q: Which is equal to 10^3?

it.h: How many places does each digit move when you multiply by 1,000?

it.q: In 4.44, the 4 in the ones place is how many times the value of the 4 in the tenths place?
it.h: Each place is 10 times the place to its right.

it.q: Explain why 2.5 x 10^2 = 250.
it.ans: 10^2 = 100. Multiplying by 100 makes each digit 100 times as large, so each digit shifts two places to the left: 2 ones become 2 hundreds and 5 tenths become 5 tens, which is 250.

lessons.u: Module 1: Place value and decimal fractions
lessons.n: Reading, writing and comparing decimals to thousandths

it.q: Which is the word form of 4.208?
ch: four and two hundred eight thousandths
four and two hundred eight hundredths
it.h: The last digit is in the thousandths place.

it.q: Which shows 3.072 in expanded form?
it.h: Name the place of each digit first.

it.q: Which symbol makes 0.405 __ 0.45 true?
it.h: Compare the hundredths digits: 0 hundredths and 5 hundredths.

it.q: Write 6 + 0.3 + 0.009 as a decimal.
it.h: There are no hundredths. What digit goes in the hundredths place?

it.q: Order from least to greatest: 2.31, 2.103, 2.13
it.h: All three have 2 ones. Compare the tenths, then the hundredths.

it.q: Explain why 0.7 > 0.698 even though 0.698 has more digits.
it.ans: Compare place by place, starting with the greatest place. 0.7 has 7 tenths and 0.698 has only 6 tenths, so 0.7 is greater. The number of digits does not decide the size.

lessons.u: Module 1: Place value and decimal fractions
lessons.n: Rounding decimals

it.q: Round 3.47 to the nearest tenth.
it.h: Look at the hundredths digit.

it.q: Round 12.649 to the nearest hundredth.
it.h: Look at the thousandths digit.

it.q: Round 7.952 to the nearest tenth.
it.h: 7.952 is between 7.9 and 8.0. Which is it closer to?

it.q: Round 0.385 to the nearest hundredth.
it.h: 0.385 is exactly halfway between 0.38 and 0.39.

it.q: Which number rounds to 4.6 when rounded to the nearest tenth?
it.h: Numbers from 4.55 up to, but not including, 4.65 round to 4.6.

it.q: Explain how a number line helps you round 2.738 to the nearest hundredth.
it.ans: 2.738 is between 2.73 and 2.74, and the halfway point is 2.735. 2.738 is past the halfway point, so it rounds to 2.74.

lessons.u: Module 1: Place value and decimal fractions
lessons.n: Adding and subtracting decimals

it.h: Line up the decimal points. You can write 4.7 as 4.70.
Write 6.2 as 6.20 before you subtract.
Write 12.06 as 12.060 so both numbers have thousandths.
Write 10 as 10.00 and rename.

it.q: Which is the best estimate for 8.92 + 3.1?
it.h: Round each number to the nearest whole number.

it.q: Explain why you line up the decimal points when you add 3.4 + 1.25.
it.ans: Lining up the decimal points lines up digits with the same place value: ones with ones and tenths with tenths. Then 3.40 + 1.25 = 4.65.

lessons.u: Module 1: Place value and decimal fractions
lessons.n: Multiplying and dividing decimals by one-digit whole numbers

it.h: 3 groups of 4 tenths is 12 tenths.
Multiply 4 by 2 ones, 1 tenth and 5 hundredths, then add.
Share 6 ones and 3 tenths into 3 equal groups.
Rename the extra ones as tenths: 7.2 is 72 tenths.

it.q: Which is the best estimate for 6 x 3.92?
it.h: Round 3.92 to the nearest whole number.

it.q: A pack of 5 markers costs $6.25. How many dollars does one marker cost?
it.h: Share $6.25 equally into 5 groups.

it.q: Explain how 4 x 0.3 is related to 4 x 3.
it.ans: 4 x 3 = 12, so 4 x 3 tenths = 12 tenths. 12 tenths is 1.2, so 4 x 0.3 = 1.2.

lessons.u: Module 2: Multi-digit whole number and decimal fraction operations
lessons.n: Expressions and mental multiplication strategies

it.h: Work inside the parentheses first, then multiply, then add.

it.q: Which expression means "add 8 and 7, then multiply by 3"?
it.h: Parentheses show which step happens first.
4 tens x 3 hundreds = 12 thousands.
Think 25 x 4 = 100, and 16 is 4 x 4.

it.q: How does the value of 4 x (12 + 9) compare with the value of 12 + 9?
it.h: You do not need to compute. What does multiplying the sum by 4 do?

it.q: Explain how to multiply 99 x 7 mentally.
it.ans: 99 is 1 less than 100. 100 x 7 = 700, then take away one 7: 700 - 7 = 693.

lessons.u: Module 2: Multi-digit whole number and decimal fraction operations
lessons.n: Multi-digit multiplication with the standard algorithm

it.h: Multiply 312 by 4, then by 20, then add the partial products.
Multiply by 3 ones, then by 1 ten, then add.
Estimate first: about 50 x 90.

it.q: Which partial products are added to find 234 x 56?
it.h: Find 234 x 6 and 234 x 50.

it.q: A theater has 38 rows with 27 seats in each row. 950 tickets were sold for a show. How many seats are empty?
it.h: First find the total number of seats.

it.q: Explain why the second row of the standard algorithm for 47 x 32 has a 0 in the ones place.
it.ans: The second row multiplies 47 by 3 tens, not 3 ones. 47 x 30 = 1,410, which has 0 ones, so the 0 holds the ones place.

lessons.u: Module 2: Multi-digit whole number and decimal fraction operations
lessons.n: Multiplying decimals by whole numbers and measurement problems

it.h: Find 24 x 13, then think about how many tenths that is.
36 hundredths x 25 = 900 hundredths.

it.q: Ribbon costs $1.75 per meter. How many dollars do 12 meters of ribbon cost?
it.h: Multiply 1.75 by 12, or find 12 x 1 and 12 x 0.75.

it.q: How many centimeters are in 3.5 meters?
it.h: 1 meter = 100 centimeters.

it.q: Which is equal to 4.2 x 30?
it.h: Think 42 tenths x 3 tens.

it.q: A runner runs 2.75 km each day for 14 days. How many kilometers does she run in all?
it.h: Estimate first: about 3 x 14.

it.q: Explain how you can use 6 x 42 to find 0.6 x 42.

lessons.u: Module 2: Multi-digit whole number and decimal fraction operations
lessons.n: Dividing whole numbers by two-digit divisors

it.h: Think 48 tens / 6 tens.
Estimate: 21 is close to 20, and 672 is close to 600 or 700.
Estimate with 40 and adjust if the product is too large or too small.
Find the largest multiple of 24 that is not more than 395.

it.q: Which is the best estimate for 3,612 / 58?
it.h: Use compatible numbers: 3,600 and 60.

it.q: Explain how to check that 2,314 / 26 = 89 is correct.
it.ans: Multiply the quotient by the divisor: 89 x 26 = 2,314. Since the product equals the dividend, the quotient is correct.

lessons.u: Module 2: Multi-digit whole number and decimal fraction operations
lessons.n: Dividing decimals and measurement word problems

it.h: 4.8 is 48 tenths. Divide 48 tenths by 12.
7.65 is 765 hundredths.
Estimate first: about 25 / 20.

it.q: Which is equal to 0.96 / 32?
it.h: 96 hundredths / 32 = how many hundredths?

it.q: A board 9.6 meters long is cut into 16 equal pieces. How many meters long is each piece?
it.h: Think 96 tenths / 16.

it.q: Explain why 3.6 / 12 has the same digit as 36 / 12 but a different value.
it.ans: 3.6 is 36 tenths, and 36 tenths / 12 = 3 tenths. The digit matches 36 / 12 = 3, but the answer is in tenths, so it is 0.3.

lessons.u: Module 2: Multi-digit whole number and decimal fraction operations
lessons.n: Estimating products and quotients to check reasonableness

it.q: Which is the best estimate of 48 x 21?
it.h: Round each factor to a number that is easy to multiply.

it.q: Round each factor to the nearest ten to estimate 62 x 38. What is the estimate?
it.h: 62 rounds to 60. What does 38 round to?

it.q: Which is the best estimate of 3,580 / 42?
it.h: Use compatible numbers that divide easily.

it.q: A school buys 29 boxes of markers with 12 markers in each box. Estimate the number of markers by rounding 29 to the nearest ten.
it.h: 29 is close to 30.

it.q: Jamal found 412 x 19 = 3,828. Which estimate shows his answer is not reasonable?
ch: 400 x 20 = 8,000, so 3,828 is far too small
it.h: Round 412 and 19, then multiply.

it.q: Explain why 4,175 / 53 must be less than 100.
it.ans: 53 x 100 = 5,300, which is more than 4,175. So fewer than 100 groups of 53 fit into 4,175, and the quotient is less than 100 (about 4,000 / 50 = 80).

lessons.u: Module 3: Addition and subtraction of fractions
lessons.n: Equivalent fractions and common denominators

it.q: 3/4 = ?/20. What is the missing numerator?
it.h: What do you multiply 4 by to get 20? Multiply the numerator by the same number.

it.q: Which denominator could you use to add 1/6 and 3/8?
it.h: Find a number that is a multiple of both 6 and 8.

it.q: Which fraction is equivalent to 2/3 and has a denominator of 15?
Which is 18/24 in simplest form?
it.h: Find the greatest number that divides both 18 and 24.

it.q: What is the least common denominator for 1/4 and 5/6?
it.h: List multiples of 6 and find the first one that is also a multiple of 4.

it.q: Explain how to rename 1/3 and 1/4 so they have the same denominator.
it.ans: Find a common multiple of 3 and 4, such as 12. Then 1/3 = 4/12 and 1/4 = 3/12, because you multiply the numerator and denominator of each fraction by the same number.

lessons.u: Module 3: Addition and subtraction of fractions
lessons.n: Adding fractions with unlike denominators

it.h: Rename both fractions as sixths.
Use 20 as a common denominator.
Use 24 as a common denominator.

it.q: Which is a correct first step for finding 2/3 + 1/6?
it.h: How many sixths are equal to 2/3?

it.q: Ivy painted 1/3 of a fence on Monday and 2/5 of it on Tuesday. What fraction of the fence has she painted?
it.h: Rename both fractions as fifteenths.

it.q: Explain why 1/2 + 1/4 is not 2/6.
it.ans: Halves and fourths are different-sized pieces, so you cannot just add the numerators and the denominators. Rename 1/2 as 2/4, then 2/4 + 1/4 = 3/4.

lessons.u: Module 3: Addition and subtraction of fractions
lessons.n: Subtracting fractions with unlike denominators

it.h: Rename both fractions as twelfths.
Use 12 as a common denominator.
How many tenths are equal to 1/2?

it.q: Which is a correct way to find 4/5 - 1/2?
it.h: Rename both fractions as tenths.

it.q: A jug holds 9/10 liter of juice. Tom drinks 1/4 liter. How many liters of juice are left in the jug?
it.h: Use 20 as a common denominator.

it.q: Explain how you can use addition to check that 5/8 - 1/4 = 3/8.
it.ans: Add the answer to the amount subtracted: 3/8 + 1/4 = 3/8 + 2/8 = 5/8. Because the sum is the starting amount, the subtraction is correct.

lessons.u: Module 3: Addition and subtraction of fractions
lessons.n: Mixed numbers, estimation and word problems

it.h: Add the wholes, then add the fractions using sixths.
Rename with twelfths. If there are not enough twelfths, rename 1 whole.

it.q: Which is a reasonable estimate for 7/8 + 4/9?
it.h: Is each fraction close to 0, 1/2 or 1?

it.q: Sam says 3/5 + 1/2 = 4/7. Which reasoning shows he is wrong?
ch: 3/5 is more than 1/2, so the sum must be more than 1, but 4/7 is less than 1
it.h: Compare each fraction with the benchmark 1/2.

it.q: A board is 6 2/3 feet long. A piece 2 3/4 feet long is cut off. How many feet long is the board now?
it.h: Rename with twelfths, then rename 1 whole if you need more twelfths.

it.q: Explain how you know 2 7/8 + 3 1/10 is about 6.
it.ans: 2 7/8 is close to 3 and 3 1/10 is close to 3, so the sum is about 3 + 3 = 6.

lessons.u: Module 3: Addition and subtraction of fractions
lessons.n: Multi-step fraction word problems with tape diagrams

it.q: Kenji has 3/4 hour to finish homework. Math takes 1/3 hour. How many hours are left for reading?
it.h: Draw a tape for 3/4 hour and mark the part used for math. Rename both fractions as twelfths.

it.q: A path is 2 1/2 miles long. Priya has walked 1 3/5 miles. How many more miles must she walk to finish?
it.h: Rename with tenths. Do you need to rename 1 whole?

it.q: A class raised money for a trip. 1/2 of the money came from a bake sale and 1/5 came from a car wash. The rest came from a book fair. What fraction came from the book fair?
it.h: First find the part that came from the bake sale and car wash together.

it.q: Ana's dog eats 2/3 cup of food in the morning and 3/4 cup at night. A bag has 10 cups of food. How many cups are left after one day?
it.h: Find the total for one day, then subtract it from 10.

it.q: A jar has 7/8 cup of rice. After Ezra uses some, 1/3 cup is left. Which equation finds the amount r he used?
it.h: Start with 7/8, take away the part used, and 1/3 is what is left.

it.q: Write a two-step word problem that can be solved with 4 - 1 1/2 - 3/4. Then solve it.
it.ans: Example: Leo has 4 feet of string. He cuts 1 1/2 feet for a kite and 3/4 foot for a bracelet. How much is left? 4 - 1 2/4 = 2 2/4, and 2 2/4 - 3/4 = 1 3/4 feet.

lessons.u: Module 3: Addition and subtraction of fractions
lessons.n: Solving for unknown amounts in fraction equations

it.q: 1/4 + ? = 5/6. What is the missing fraction?
it.h: Subtract 1/4 from 5/6 using twelfths.

it.q: ? - 2/5 = 1/3. What is the missing fraction?
it.h: Add 2/5 and 1/3 to undo the subtraction.

it.q: Kim had some milk. She drank 1/3 cup and has 1/2 cup left. Which equation finds how much milk m she started with?
it.h: She started with m and took away 1/3.

it.q: A trail is 3/4 mile long. Rico walked 1/6 mile, rested, then walked 1/3 mile. How much farther must he walk to finish the trail?
it.h: Write an equation with a missing part, and use twelfths.

it.q: 7/8 - ? = 1/2. What is the missing fraction?
it.h: How far is it from 1/2 up to 7/8?

it.q: Explain how you can use addition to find the missing number in ? - 3/10 = 1/2.
it.ans: The missing number is the starting amount. Add back the part taken away: 1/2 + 3/10 = 5/10 + 3/10 = 8/10. Check: 8/10 - 3/10 = 5/10 = 1/2.

lessons.u: Module 3: Addition and subtraction of fractions
lessons.n: Fraction measurement problems with time, length and weight

it.q: Ari practiced piano for 1/2 hour and guitar for 1/3 hour. How many minutes did he practice in all?
it.h: How many minutes are in 1/2 hour? In 1/3 hour?

it.q: One board is 3/4 foot long and another is 2/3 foot long. How many inches longer is the first board? (1 foot = 12 inches)
it.h: Change each length to inches.

it.q: What is the total of 1/4 hour and 1/6 hour?
it.h: Use twelfths.

it.q: One package weighs 1 1/2 pounds and another weighs 3/4 pound. How many pounds do they weigh together?
it.h: Rename 1/2 as fourths.

it.q: Mei's bus ride takes 3/4 hour and her walk from the bus takes 1/6 hour. She must arrive by 8:00 a.m. What is the latest she can leave, in minutes after 7:00 a.m.?
it.h: Find the total travel time in minutes first.

it.q: Explain why 2/3 of an hour and 40 minutes are the same amount of time.
it.ans: One hour is 60 minutes. 1/3 of 60 is 20, so 2/3 of an hour is 2 x 20 = 40 minutes.

lessons.u: Module 4: Multiplication and division of fractions and decimal fractions
lessons.n: Fractions as division and fraction line plots

it.q: 3 pizzas are shared equally by 4 friends. How much pizza does each friend get?
it.h: Divide the number of pizzas by the number of friends.

it.q: 7 / 2 = ? Write the answer as a mixed number.
it.h: How many whole 2s are in 7? What fraction is left?

it.q: Which division expression is equal to 5/8?
it.h: A fraction bar means "divided by".

it.q: 10 yards of ribbon are cut into 4 equal pieces. How many yards long is each piece?
it.h: Divide 10 by 4 and write the remainder as a fraction.

it.q: A line plot shows rope lengths: 2 ropes are 1/4 foot, 3 ropes are 1/2 foot and 1 rope is 3/4 foot. All six ropes are joined end to end. How many feet long is the joined rope?
it.h: Multiply each length by the number of ropes, then add.

it.q: Use 2 sandwiches shared equally by 3 people to explain why 2 / 3 = 2/3.
it.ans: Cut each sandwich into thirds, which makes 6 thirds. Each person gets 2 of the 6 thirds, so each person gets 2/3 of a sandwich.

lessons.u: Module 4: Multiplication and division of fractions and decimal fractions
lessons.n: Multiplying a whole number by a fraction

it.h: Find 1/3 of 12 first, then double it.

it.q: In a class of 20 students, 3/4 ride the bus. How many students ride the bus?
it.h: Find 1/4 of 20, then multiply by 3.
5 groups of 2 thirds is how many thirds?

it.q: Which expression shows 2/5 of 30?
it.h: "Of" means multiply.

it.q: Mr. Kim had 48 cookies. He gave 1/4 of them to one class and 1/3 of them to another class. How many cookies are left?
it.h: Find 1/4 of 48 and 1/3 of 48 first.

it.q: Explain how a tape diagram shows 3/5 of 25.
it.ans: Split a bar that stands for 25 into 5 equal parts; each part is 25 / 5 = 5. Three parts are 3 x 5 = 15, so 3/5 of 25 is 15.

lessons.u: Module 4: Multiplication and division of fractions and decimal fractions
lessons.n: Multiplying fractions by fractions and decimals by decimals

it.h: Find half of one third.
Multiply the numerators, then multiply the denominators.
4 tenths x 3 tenths = 12 hundredths.
Think 15 tenths x 6 tenths = 90 hundredths.

it.q: A rug is 3/4 yard long and 1/2 yard wide. What is its area?
it.h: Area is length times width.

it.q: Describe an area model for 2/3 x 4/5 and use it to find the product.
it.ans: Draw a square split into 3 rows and 5 columns, making 15 equal parts. Shade 2 rows and 4 columns; the overlap is 8 parts, so 2/3 x 4/5 = 8/15.

lessons.u: Module 4: Multiplication and division of fractions and decimal fractions
lessons.n: Multiplication as scaling

it.q: Without multiplying, which product is less than 8?
it.h: What happens when you multiply by a number less than 1?

it.q: Which statement about 2/3 x 15 is true?
it.h: 2/3 is less than 1.

it.q: A photo 4 inches wide is enlarged to 1 1/2 times its width. How many inches wide is the new photo?
it.h: 1 1/2 times 4 is 4 plus half of 4.

it.q: Which is greater, 7/8 x 12 or 9/8 x 12?
it.h: Compare 7/8 and 9/8 with 1.

it.q: A recipe uses 2 1/2 cups of flour. Ken makes 3/4 of the recipe. How many cups of flour does he use?
it.h: Write 2 1/2 as 5/2, then multiply by 3/4.

it.q: Explain why 5 x 0.9 is a little less than 5.
it.ans: 0.9 is a little less than 1. Multiplying 5 by 1 keeps it 5, so multiplying by a little less than 1 gives a little less than 5. The product is 4.5.

lessons.u: Module 4: Multiplication and division of fractions and decimal fractions
lessons.n: Dividing with unit fractions and decimals

it.h: How many fourths are in 3 wholes?
Split one half into 4 equal parts.
How many groups of 3 tenths are in 12 tenths?
How many halves are in 5?

it.q: How many 1/3-cup servings are in 4 cups of rice?
it.h: Each cup has 3 servings.

it.q: 3 friends share 1/2 of a pizza equally. What fraction of the whole pizza does each friend get?
it.h: Split one half into 3 equal parts.

it.q: Explain why 2 / (1/5) = 10.
it.ans: 1/5 fits into 1 whole 5 times, so it fits into 2 wholes 2 x 5 = 10 times.

lessons.u: Module 4: Multiplication and division of fractions and decimal fractions
lessons.n: Multiplying mixed numbers in real-world problems

it.h: Multiply 4 by 2 and 4 by 1/2, then add.

it.q: A recipe uses 1 1/3 cups of oats. How many cups of oats are needed for 3 batches?
it.h: Multiply each part of the mixed number by 3.

it.q: Which is equal to 1 1/2 x 2/3?
it.h: Write 1 1/2 as 3/2.

it.q: A garden bed is 3 1/2 feet long and 2 feet wide. What is its area in square feet?
it.h: Area = length x width.

it.q: Ana walks 1 3/4 miles each day. How many miles does she walk in 6 days?
it.h: 6 x 1 = 6. What is 6 x 3/4?

it.q: Explain why 3 x 1 1/4 is greater than 3 but 1/2 x 1 1/4 is less than 1 1/4.
it.ans: 1 1/4 is greater than 1, so 3 groups of 1 1/4 is more than 3 groups of 1 (it is 3 3/4). 1/2 is less than 1, so half of 1 1/4 is less than 1 1/4 (it is 5/8).

lessons.u: Module 4: Multiplication and division of fractions and decimal fractions
lessons.n: Multi-step fraction and decimal problems with recipes, money and measurement

it.q: A recipe for 4 people uses 3/4 cup of rice. How many cups of rice are needed for 8 people?
it.h: 8 people is how many times as many as 4 people?

it.q: Juice costs $0.85 per bottle. Ken buys 6 bottles and pays with a $10 bill. How much change does he get, in dollars?
it.h: Find the cost first, then subtract it from 10.

it.q: A 3-pound bag of nuts is split into small bags of 1/4 pound each. How many small bags are there?
it.h: How many fourths are in 1 whole? In 3 wholes?

it.q: Maria buys 2 1/2 pounds of apples at $2 per pound and 1/2 pound of cheese at $6 per pound. How many dollars does she spend?
it.h: Find each cost and add.

it.q: A ribbon 5 meters long is cut into pieces that are each 1/3 meter long. How many pieces are there?
it.h: Each meter makes 3 pieces.

it.q: Explain how to find the cost of 3/4 pound of turkey at $8 per pound.
it.ans: Find 3/4 of 8. 1/4 of 8 is 2, so 3/4 of 8 is 3 x 2 = 6. The turkey costs $6.

lessons.u: Module 5: Addition and multiplication with volume and area
lessons.n: Understanding volume with unit cubes

it.q: Which unit could be used to measure volume?
it.h: Volume measures how much space a solid takes up.

it.q: A box is filled with 3 layers of cubes. Each layer has 8 cubes. How many cubes fill the box?
it.h: Multiply the cubes in one layer by the number of layers.

it.q: A rectangular prism is built from unit cubes. It is 5 cubes long, 2 cubes wide and 3 cubes tall. What is its volume in cubic units?
it.h: Find the cubes in one layer first.

it.q: Why can't volume be measured in square units?
ch: Square units are flat and cannot fill space
it.h: Think about what a square unit covers and what a cube fills.

it.q: A cube has edges 3 cm long. How many 1-centimeter cubes fill it?
it.h: Each layer is 3 by 3, and there are 3 layers.

it.q: Explain why packing a box with gaps between the cubes gives the wrong volume.
it.ans: Volume is the number of unit cubes that fill a space with no gaps or overlaps. If there are gaps, the box is not filled, so the count is too small.

lessons.u: Module 5: Addition and multiplication with volume and area
lessons.n: Volume formulas and composite solids

it.q: Use V = l x w x h. A box is 7 inches long, 4 inches wide and 3 inches tall. What is its volume in cubic inches?
it.h: Multiply the three dimensions.

it.q: A box has a base area of 18 square feet and a height of 5 feet. What is its volume in cubic feet?
it.h: Volume = base area x height.

it.q: A box has a volume of 60 cubic inches, a length of 5 inches and a width of 3 inches. What is its height in inches?
it.h: First find the base area, then think: base area x ? = 60.

it.q: A solid is made of a 4 by 3 by 2 prism and a 2 by 2 by 5 prism. What is its total volume?
it.h: Find the volume of each prism, then add.

it.q: An aquarium is 50 cm long, 20 cm wide and 30 cm tall. Water fills it to a depth of 25 cm. How many cubic centimeters of water are in it?
it.h: Use the water's depth, not the tank's height.

it.q: Explain why V = b x h works for a rectangular prism.
it.ans: The base area b tells how many unit cubes fit in one layer, and the height h tells how many layers there are, so b x h counts all the cubes.

lessons.u: Module 5: Addition and multiplication with volume and area
lessons.n: Area with fractional side lengths

it.q: A rectangle is 3 1/2 feet by 4 feet. What is its area in square feet?
it.h: Find 3 x 4 and 1/2 x 4, then add.

it.q: A tile is 2/3 foot by 3/4 foot. What is its area in square feet?
it.h: Multiply the numerators and the denominators.

it.q: A garden is 5 1/2 m by 2 1/4 m. What is its area in square meters?
it.h: Write each side as a fraction greater than 1, or use partial products.

it.q: Which expression finds the area of a 2 1/2 by 3 1/3 rectangle using partial products?
it.h: Each part of one side must be multiplied by each part of the other side.

it.q: A wall is 8 feet wide and 9 1/2 feet tall. It has a door that is 3 feet by 6 2/3 feet. How many square feet of the wall need paint?
it.h: Find the wall's area and the door's area, then subtract.

it.q: Explain how tiling a 1 1/2 by 2 1/2 rectangle shows its area.
it.ans: Whole unit squares cover 1 by 2 = 2 square units. The strips along the edges cover 1 x 1/2 = 1/2 and 1/2 x 2 = 1. The corner piece is 1/2 x 1/2 = 1/4. The total is 3 3/4 square units, the same as 3/2 x 5/2 = 15/4.

lessons.u: Module 5: Addition and multiplication with volume and area
lessons.n: Classifying two-dimensional figures

it.q: Which quadrilateral always has 4 right angles but does not need 4 equal sides?
it.h: Which shape is named for its right angles?

it.q: Which statement is always true?
it.h: Check whether a square has every attribute of a rectangle.

it.q: A parallelogram has 4 equal sides. What else must it be?
ch: a quadrilateral with no parallel sides
it.h: Which shape is defined by 4 equal sides?

it.q: Which attribute do all parallelograms have?
ch: opposite sides are parallel and equal in length
only one pair of parallel sides
it.h: Think about rectangles, rhombuses and squares, which are all parallelograms.

it.q: How many pairs of parallel sides does a parallelogram have?
it.h: Look at both pairs of opposite sides.

it.q: Explain why a square is also a rhombus.
it.ans: A rhombus is a quadrilateral with 4 equal sides. A square has 4 equal sides, so it is a rhombus. It also has 4 right angles, which makes it a special rhombus.

lessons.u: Module 5: Addition and multiplication with volume and area
lessons.n: Volume word problems with unknown dimensions and filling containers

it.q: A toy box has a volume of 96 cubic feet. It is 4 feet long and 3 feet wide. How tall is it in feet?
it.h: Multiply the length by the width to find the area of the base. What times that gives 96?

it.q: A fish tank is 20 inches long, 10 inches wide and 12 inches tall. How many cubic inches of water does it hold when full?
it.h: Use V = l x w x h.

it.q: Which box holds the most?
it.h: Find the volume of each box.

it.q: A sandbox is 6 feet long, 4 feet wide and 2 feet deep. It is half full of sand. How many more cubic feet of sand will fill it?
it.h: Find the full volume first.

it.q: A box has a base with an area of 15 square centimeters and holds 75 cubic centimeters. How tall is the box in centimeters?
it.h: Volume = area of the base x height.

it.q: Two boxes each have a volume of 36 cubic units but different shapes. Give two different sets of dimensions they could have and explain how you know.
it.ans: Example: 3 x 3 x 4 = 36 and 2 x 2 x 9 = 36. Any whole-number length, width and height whose product is 36 gives a volume of 36 cubic units.

lessons.u: Module 5: Addition and multiplication with volume and area
lessons.n: Classifying triangles by sides and angles

it.q: A triangle has three sides that are all different lengths. What is it called?
it.h: Count how many sides are the same length.

it.q: A triangle has one angle that measures 90 degrees. Which name fits it?
it.h: A 90-degree angle is a square corner.

it.q: A triangle's angles measure 40, 60 and 80 degrees. How is it classified by its angles?
it.h: Are all three angles less than 90 degrees?

it.q: An equilateral triangle has one side 7 cm long. What is its perimeter in centimeters?
it.h: How many sides of an equilateral triangle are the same length?

it.q: Which statement about triangles is always true?
ch: Every equilateral triangle is also isosceles
Every isosceles triangle is also equilateral
Every right triangle is also obtuse
Every scalene triangle is also right
it.h: An isosceles triangle has at least two equal sides.

it.q: Can a triangle be both right and obtuse? Explain.
it.ans: No. A right triangle has a 90-degree angle and an obtuse triangle has an angle greater than 90 degrees. If one triangle had both, the two sides coming off the third side would spread apart and never meet, so a triangle can have only one angle of 90 degrees or more.

lessons.u: Module 6: Problem solving with the coordinate plane
lessons.n: Coordinate systems and plotting points

it.q: In the ordered pair (4, 2), what does the 4 tell you?
ch: how far to move along the x-axis from the origin
how far to move along the y-axis from the origin
the number of points on the line
it.h: The first number is the x-coordinate.

it.q: What are the coordinates of the origin?
it.h: The origin is where the two axes meet.

it.q: Start at the origin, move 3 units right and 5 units up. Which point are you at?
it.h: Write the move right first, then the move up.

it.q: Point A is at (6, 4). What is its y-coordinate?
it.h: The y-coordinate is the second number.

it.q: Which point is on the x-axis?
it.h: A point on the x-axis has not moved up at all.

it.q: Explain the difference between the points (2, 6) and (6, 2).
it.ans: (2, 6) is 2 units right and 6 units up from the origin, and (6, 2) is 6 units right and 2 units up. The order of the coordinates matters, so they are different points.

lessons.u: Module 6: Problem solving with the coordinate plane
lessons.n: Numerical patterns and graphing rules

it.q: A pattern starts at 0 and adds 3: 0, 3, 6, 9. What is the next number?
it.h: Add 3 to the last term.

it.q: Pattern A starts at 0 and adds 2. Pattern B starts at 0 and adds 4. Which statement about matching terms is true?
ch: Each term in B is twice the matching term in A
Each term in B is 2 more than the matching term in A
Each term in A is twice the matching term in B
it.h: List the first four terms of each pattern and compare.

it.q: A pattern starts at 0 and adds 5. The first term is 0. What is the fifth term?
it.h: List the terms: 0, 5, and so on.

it.q: The rule is "y is 3 more than x". Which point follows the rule?
it.h: Add 3 to the x-coordinate. Do you get the y-coordinate?

it.q: The rule is "multiply x by 2 to get y". What is y when x is 7?
it.h: Use the rule on 7.

it.q: Pattern A is 0, 3, 6, 9 and pattern B is 0, 6, 12, 18. Describe how the patterns are related and write the ordered pairs (A, B).
it.ans: Each term in pattern B is 2 times the matching term in pattern A. The ordered pairs are (0, 0), (3, 6), (6, 12) and (9, 18).

lessons.u: Module 6: Problem solving with the coordinate plane
lessons.n: Drawing figures and finding lengths on the coordinate plane

it.q: A rectangle has corners at (1, 1), (6, 1), (6, 4) and (1, 4). How many units long is its horizontal side?
it.h: Subtract the x-coordinates of two corners on the same horizontal side.

it.q: A rectangle has corners at (1, 1), (6, 1), (6, 4) and (1, 4). What is its area in square units?
it.h: Find the length and the width first.

it.q: Three corners of a square are (2, 2), (5, 2) and (5, 5). What is the fourth corner?
it.h: Sketch the three points. Which corner is missing?

it.q: A rectangle has corners at (0, 0), (8, 0), (8, 3) and (0, 3). What is its perimeter in units?
it.h: Find the length and width, then add all four sides.

it.q: A line goes through (3, 0) and (3, 7). Which statement describes the line?
ch: It is parallel to the y-axis
It is parallel to the x-axis
It slants up to the right
it.h: Both points have the same x-coordinate.

it.q: Explain how you know a line through (1, 4) and (9, 4) is parallel to the x-axis.
it.ans: Both points have a y-coordinate of 4, so every point on the line is 4 units above the x-axis. The line stays the same distance from the x-axis, so it is parallel to it.

lessons.u: Module 6: Problem solving with the coordinate plane
lessons.n: Problem solving with the coordinate plane

it.q: A town map shows the school at (2, 3) and the library at (2, 8). Each unit is 1 block. How many blocks apart are they?
it.h: The x-coordinates match, so subtract the y-coordinates.

it.q: A taxi charges $3 plus $2 for each mile. Its graph of (miles, cost) includes (1, 5), (2, 7) and (3, 9). How many dollars does a 6-mile ride cost?
it.h: Each extra mile adds $2.

it.q: A graph of a bike ride shows the points (1, 12), (2, 24) and (3, 36) as (hours, miles). Which rule fits the graph?
it.h: How do the miles change each hour?

it.q: Leo walks from (1, 1) to (1, 5), then to (6, 5). Each unit is 100 meters. How many meters does he walk?
it.h: Find each part of the walk in units, then convert.

it.q: Jo has $10 saved and saves $5 more each week. Which point shows (week, dollars) for week 4?
it.h: Start at 10 and add 5 four times.

it.q: Explain how a graph of (weeks, dollars saved) can help you predict savings for a later week.
it.ans: The points follow a rule and line up, so you can continue the pattern or extend the line to read the number of dollars for a later week.

lessons.u: Module 6: Problem solving with the coordinate plane
lessons.n: Line graphs of real-world data on the coordinate plane

it.q: A line graph shows a puppy's weight. The points are (1, 4), (2, 6), (3, 9) and (4, 11), where x is the month and y is the weight in pounds. How many pounds did the puppy gain from month 1 to month 4?
it.h: Subtract the y-coordinate at month 1 from the y-coordinate at month 4.

it.q: A graph of the temperature in a garden has the points (6, 52), (8, 58), (10, 65) and (12, 70), where x is the hour of the morning and y is the temperature in degrees F. Between which two hours did the temperature rise the most?
ch: It rose the same amount each time
it.h: Find the change in y between each pair of points.

it.q: Maya starts with $0 and saves $5 each week. Her savings are graphed with x as the week and y as the dollars saved. What is the y-coordinate of the point for week 6?
it.h: Multiply the number of weeks by 5.

it.q: A graph shows the points (0, 0), (1, 3), (2, 6) and (3, 9) for the number of laps (y) a swimmer finishes after x minutes. If the pattern continues, which point shows the laps after 5 minutes?
it.h: Each minute adds the same number of laps.

it.q: A plant's height in centimeters (y) is graphed against the week (x). The points are (0, 3), (1, 5), (2, 7) and (3, 9). If the pattern continues, in which week will the plant be 15 centimeters tall?
it.h: How much does the plant grow each week?

it.q: Explain what the point (4, 20) means on a graph where x is hours worked and y is dollars earned.
it.ans: After working 4 hours, the person has earned 20 dollars. The x-coordinate tells the hours and the y-coordinate tells the money.

lessons.u: Module 1: Ratios and unit rates
lessons.n: Ratios and equivalent ratios

it.q: A class has 12 girls and 15 boys. What is the ratio of boys to girls?
it.h: The order of the words tells you the order of the numbers.

it.q: Which ratio is equivalent to 3:5?
it.h: Multiply both numbers in the ratio by the same number.

it.q: A juice mix uses 2 cups of mango juice for every 7 cups of water. How many cups of water go with 6 cups of mango juice?
it.h: How many times bigger is 6 than 2?

it.q: In a garden, the ratio of tomato plants to pepper plants is 4:3. There are 28 plants in all. How many tomato plants are there?
it.h: There are 4 + 3 = 7 parts in all. How many plants are in one part?

it.q: A team has 5 forwards for every 2 goalies. Which could be the numbers of forwards and goalies on the team?
it.h: Check whether both numbers were multiplied by the same number.

it.q: Explain what the ratio 5:2 means for a team that has 5 forwards for every 2 goalies. Give one other pair of numbers with the same ratio.
it.ans: For every 5 forwards there are 2 goalies. For example, 10 forwards and 4 goalies keep the same ratio because both numbers are doubled.

lessons.u: Module 1: Ratios and unit rates
lessons.n: Ratio tables, tape diagrams and graphs

it.q: A ratio table shows 2 laps in 5 minutes, 4 laps in 10 minutes and 6 laps in 15 minutes. How many minutes does it take to run 10 laps?
it.h: Add two rows of the table together, or find the time for 1 lap.

it.q: The ratio of x to y is 1:3. Which point would be on the graph of these equivalent ratios?
it.h: The y-value should be 3 times the x-value.

it.q: A tape diagram shows Kenji's stamps as 4 equal boxes and Rosa's stamps as 7 boxes of the same size. Rosa has 21 more stamps than Kenji. How many stamps does Kenji have?
it.h: The difference is how many boxes? What is one box worth?

it.q: Which table shows equivalent ratios?
it.h: Look for a number you multiply by to get from one row to the next.

it.q: Two numbers are in the ratio 3:8 and their sum is 77. What is the larger number?
it.h: Draw 3 boxes and 8 boxes. What is one box worth?

lessons.u: Module 1: Ratios and unit rates
lessons.n: Unit rates and rate problems

it.q: A car travels 240 miles on 8 gallons of gas. How many miles per gallon is that?
it.h: Divide to find the distance for 1 gallon.

it.q: Which is the better buy for rice?
ch: Both have the same unit price
You cannot tell without more information
it.h: Find the price of 1 pound for each choice.

it.q: Ayesha types 345 words in 5 minutes. At this rate, how many words does she type in 12 minutes?
it.h: First find how many words she types in 1 minute.

it.q: How many inches are in 4.5 feet?
it.h: 1 foot = 12 inches.

it.q: A printer prints 84 pages in 6 minutes. What is its unit rate?
Explain how "3 feet per second" and "1/3 second per foot" describe the same situation.
it.ans: Both come from the ratio 3 feet : 1 second. One tells the distance in 1 second and the other tells the time for 1 foot.

lessons.u: Module 1: Ratios and unit rates
lessons.n: Percent

it.q: What is 3/5 written as a percent?
it.h: Write an equivalent fraction with a denominator of 100.

it.q: What is 25% of 64?
it.h: 25% is the same as 1/4.

it.q: Which decimal equals 7%?
it.h: Percent means "out of 100".

it.q: 18 is 30% of what number?
it.h: If 30% is 18, what is 10%? What is 100%?

it.q: A class has 25 students and 40% of them walk to school. How many students walk?
Explain how a 10 by 10 grid can show 45%.
it.ans: The grid has 100 squares. Shade 45 of them; 45 out of 100 is 45%.

lessons.u: Module 1: Ratios and unit rates
lessons.n: Converting measurement units with ratios

it.q: There are 12 inches in 1 foot. How many inches are in 7 feet?
it.h: Each foot adds 12 inches.

it.q: There are 3 feet in 1 yard. A garden hose is 75 feet long. How many yards long is it?
it.h: How many groups of 3 feet are in 75 feet?

it.q: There are 16 ounces in 1 pound. Which pair of measurements is equal?
it.h: Multiply both parts of the ratio 1 : 16 by the same number.

it.q: There are 1,000 meters in 1 kilometer. A race is 5 kilometers long. How many meters long is it?
it.h: Use the ratio 1 kilometer : 1,000 meters.

it.q: A soup recipe needs 3 quarts of broth. Broth is sold in cans that hold 1 cup, and 1 quart = 4 cups. How many cans are needed?
it.h: Change quarts to cups first.

it.q: Explain why you multiply to convert hours to minutes but divide to convert minutes to hours.
it.ans: Each hour is 60 minutes, so a number of hours is worth 60 times as many minutes; multiply by 60. Minutes are the smaller unit, so to find how many groups of 60 minutes there are, divide by 60.

lessons.u: Module 1: Ratios and unit rates
lessons.n: Finding the whole from a part and a percent

it.q: 12 is 25% of what number?
it.h: 25% is 1/4. 12 is one fourth of the whole.

it.q: 9 students in a class walk to school. That is 30% of the class. How many students are in the class?
it.h: If 30% is 9, what is 10%?

it.q: A team won 18 games, which is 60% of the games it played. Which reasoning finds the number of games played?
ch: 6 parts of 10% make 18, so each part is 3 and 10 parts are 30
it.h: Split 100% into 10 equal parts of 10%.

it.q: A jar has 40 red beads. The red beads are 80% of the beads in the jar. How many beads are in the jar?
it.h: Find 10% first.

it.q: Leo has saved $45, which is 75% of the cost of a bike helmet. How many more dollars does he need to buy the helmet?
it.h: First find the full cost of the helmet.

it.q: Explain how a double number line helps you find the whole when 20% of it is 14.
it.ans: Mark 0% across from 0 and 20% across from 14. 100% is 5 jumps of 20%, so the whole is 5 x 14 = 70. Each 20% jump on the percent line matches a jump of 14 on the number line.

lessons.u: Module 1: Ratios and unit rates
lessons.n: Comparing ratios and rates with tables and graphs

it.q: Lemonade A uses 2 cups of mix for 6 cups of water. Lemonade B uses 3 cups of mix for 12 cups of water. Which tastes stronger?
ch: A, because it has 1 cup of mix for every 3 cups of water
B, because it uses more mix
B, because it has 1 cup of mix for every 4 cups of water
it.h: Find the cups of water for 1 cup of mix in each.

it.q: Ali reads 45 pages in 3 hours. Bea reads 64 pages in 4 hours. How many more pages per hour does Bea read?
it.h: Find each unit rate.

it.q: A graph shows two lines through (0, 0). Line A passes through (2, 10). Line B passes through (3, 12). Which line shows the greater rate?
ch: Line B, because 12 is more than 10
it.h: Divide y by x for each point.

it.q: Store A sells 4 notebooks for $6. Store B sells 6 notebooks for $8.40. How many cents cheaper is one notebook at Store B?
it.h: Find the price of one notebook at each store.

it.q: Car A travels 150 miles in 3 hours. Car B travels 220 miles in 4 hours. If both keep the same speed, how many miles farther does Car B go in 6 hours?
it.h: Find each speed, then multiply by 6.

it.q: Explain how a ratio table can show whether two mixtures of blue and white paint are the same shade.
it.ans: Extend each ratio in a table until both have the same amount of one color. If the other color also matches, the ratios are equivalent and the shades are the same; if not, the one with more blue for the same white is darker.

lessons.u: Module 2: Arithmetic operations including dividing by a fraction
lessons.n: Dividing fractions by fractions

it.q: How many 1/4-cup scoops are in 3 cups?
it.h: How many fourths are in one whole? In three wholes?
How many sixths are in 2/3?
Multiply by the reciprocal of the divisor.

it.q: Which story matches 5 ÷ 1/2?
ch: How many half-mile laps make 5 miles?
5 friends share 1/2 of a pizza. How much does each get?
A 1/2-mile trail is walked 5 times. How far is that?
it.h: Dividing by 1/2 asks how many halves fit into 5.

it.q: A ribbon is 7/8 yard long. It is cut into pieces that are each 1/8 yard long. How many pieces are there?
Describe a tape diagram or number line that shows 1 1/2 ÷ 3/4 = 2.
it.ans: Mark 1 1/2 on a number line divided into fourths; it is 6 fourths. Groups of 3 fourths fit into 6 fourths exactly 2 times.

lessons.u: Module 2: Arithmetic operations including dividing by a fraction
lessons.n: Adding, subtracting and multiplying multi-digit decimals

it.h: Line up the decimal points before adding.
Write 20 as 20.00.
Multiply 36 x 25, then count the decimal places in both factors.

it.q: Which is the best estimate for 4.92 x 6.1?
it.h: Round each factor to the nearest whole number.

it.q: Ravi buys 2.5 pounds of grapes at $3.18 per pound. How many dollars does he pay?
Explain why 0.4 x 0.3 = 0.12 and not 1.2.
it.ans: Tenths times tenths makes hundredths, so 4 tenths x 3 tenths = 12 hundredths = 0.12. It also makes sense because both factors are less than 1, so the product must be less than each factor.

lessons.u: Module 2: Arithmetic operations including dividing by a fraction
lessons.n: Dividing whole numbers and decimals

it.h: Use long division. How many 12s are in 34?
Multiply both numbers by 10 so the divisor is a whole number.
Multiply both numbers by 100.

it.q: Which division has the same quotient as 2.4 ÷ 0.08?
it.h: Multiply the dividend and the divisor by the same power of 10.

it.q: A 9.6-meter rope is cut into pieces 0.4 meter long. How many pieces are there?
Explain why 6 ÷ 0.5 is greater than 6.
it.ans: Dividing by 0.5 asks how many halves are in 6. There are 2 halves in each whole, so there are 12 halves in 6, which is greater than 6.

lessons.u: Module 2: Arithmetic operations including dividing by a fraction
lessons.n: Factors, multiples and the distributive property

it.q: What is the greatest common factor (GCF) of 18 and 30?
it.h: List the factors of each number and find the largest one they share.

it.q: What is the least common multiple (LCM) of 6 and 8?
it.h: List multiples of 8 until you find one that is also a multiple of 6.

it.q: Which expression uses the GCF to rewrite 24 + 36?
it.h: Find the greatest number that divides both 24 and 36.

it.q: Hot dogs come in packs of 10 and buns come in packs of 8. What is the fewest hot dogs you can buy to have exactly the same number of hot dogs and buns?
A teacher has 42 pencils and 56 erasers. She makes identical kits with nothing left over. What is the greatest number of kits she can make?
Explain how you can tell whether a word problem asks for a GCF or an LCM.
it.ans: GCF problems split two amounts into the greatest number of identical groups. LCM problems look for the first time two repeating events happen together, or the smallest amount that is a multiple of both.

lessons.u: Module 2: Arithmetic operations including dividing by a fraction
lessons.n: Multi-step problems with fractions and decimals

it.q: A 3/4-pound bag of trail mix is split into portions of 1/8 pound. How many portions are there?
it.h: How many eighths are in 3/4?

it.q: Ella buys 2.5 pounds of apples at $1.80 per pound and pays with a $10 bill. How much change does she get, in dollars?
it.h: Find the cost first, then subtract it from 10.

it.q: A ribbon is 4 1/2 feet long. It is cut into pieces that are 3/4 foot long. Which expression gives the number of pieces?
it.h: You are finding how many 3/4s fit into 4 1/2.

it.q: A car uses 1.25 gallons of gas each day. How many gallons does it use in 6 days?
it.h: Multiply the decimal by the number of days.

it.q: A carpenter has a board 6 2/3 feet long. She cuts off a piece 1 1/3 feet long, then cuts the rest into pieces that are 2/3 foot long. How many 2/3-foot pieces does she get?
it.h: Find the length left after the first cut, then divide.

it.q: Explain how you can check that 2 ÷ 2/5 = 5.
it.ans: Multiply the quotient by the divisor: 5 x 2/5 = 10/5 = 2. The product is the dividend, so the quotient is correct. You can also see that five pieces of 2/5 make 2 wholes.

lessons.u: Module 2: Arithmetic operations including dividing by a fraction
lessons.n: Greatest common factor and least common multiple in word problems

it.q: What is the greatest common factor of 18 and 24?
it.h: List the factors of each number.

it.q: What is the least common multiple of 6 and 8?
it.h: List multiples of 8 until one is also a multiple of 6.

it.q: Ms. Kaur has 36 pencils and 48 erasers. She wants identical kits with nothing left over. What is the greatest number of kits she can make?
it.h: Find the greatest number that divides both 36 and 48.

it.q: Hot dogs come in packs of 10 and buns in packs of 8. What is the fewest hot dogs to buy so there is exactly one bun for each hot dog with none left over?
ch: 40, the least common multiple of 10 and 8
2, the greatest common factor of 10 and 8
it.h: Do you need a common factor or a common multiple?

it.q: One light blinks every 4 seconds and another blinks every 6 seconds. They blink together right now. In how many seconds will they next blink together?
it.h: Find the least common multiple.

it.q: Explain how to use the greatest common factor to write 24 + 36 as a product with the distributive property.

lessons.u: Module 3: Rational numbers
lessons.n: Positive and negative numbers on the number line

it.q: A diver is 15 feet below the surface of the water. Which number shows her position?
it.h: Below the surface is less than zero.

it.q: What is the opposite of 8?
What is the opposite of the opposite of -6?
it.h: Find the opposite of -6 first, then take the opposite of that number.

it.q: Which situation is represented by +250?
On a number line, a point is 3 units to the left of 1. What number is it?
it.h: Start at 1 and count 3 units toward the negative numbers.

it.q: Explain what 0 means in a situation about elevation and in a situation about a bank account.
it.ans: For elevation, 0 is sea level. For a bank account, 0 means there is no money in the account and no money owed.

lessons.u: Module 3: Rational numbers
lessons.n: Ordering and comparing rational numbers

it.q: Which number is greatest?
it.h: On a number line, numbers farther to the right are greater.

it.q: Which statement comparing -4 and -1 is true?
What is the least number in this list: 0.5, -1.25, -3/4, -1.2?
it.h: Place each number on a number line.

it.q: Which list is in order from least to greatest?
Lake A is at -10 feet, Lake B is at -45 feet and Lake C is at -28 feet compared with sea level. What is the elevation of the lowest lake, in feet?
Write an inequality comparing -5 degrees and -2 degrees, and explain what it means about the temperatures.
it.ans: -5 < -2. A temperature of -5 degrees is colder than -2 degrees because it is farther below zero.

lessons.u: Module 3: Rational numbers
lessons.n: Absolute value

it.q: What is abs(-14)?
it.h: Absolute value is the distance from 0.

it.q: Which number has the greatest absolute value?
it.h: Ignore the signs and compare distances from 0.

it.q: Which statement about absolute value is true?
An account balance is -$35. How many dollars of debt does that show?
it.h: The size of the debt is the absolute value of the balance.

it.q: Which two numbers both have an absolute value of 4.5?
Explain why a balance of -$50 is less than -$20 but represents a larger debt.
it.ans: -50 is to the left of -20 on the number line, so it is less. Its absolute value, 50, is greater than 20, so it is a larger debt.

lessons.u: Module 3: Rational numbers
lessons.n: The coordinate plane

it.q: In which quadrant is the point (-3, 5)?
it.h: A negative x means left of the y-axis; a positive y means above the x-axis.

it.q: The point (4, -2) is reflected across the x-axis. What is the new point?
it.h: Reflecting across the x-axis changes the sign of the y-coordinate.

it.q: What is the distance between (2, -3) and (2, 5)?
it.h: The x-coordinates match, so find the vertical distance.

it.q: What is the distance between (-6, 1) and (4, 1)?
Which point is in Quadrant IV?
Explain how to use absolute value to find the distance between (-5, 2) and (3, 2).
it.ans: The y-coordinates match, so the distance is horizontal. The points are on opposite sides of the y-axis, 5 and 3 units away, so the distance is abs(-5) + abs(3) = 8 units.

lessons.u: Module 3: Rational numbers
lessons.n: Rational numbers in real-world contexts: temperature, elevation and money

it.q: A diver is 30 feet below sea level. Which number represents her position?
it.h: Below sea level is less than 0.

it.q: The temperature in Town A is -4 degrees F and in Town B is -11 degrees F. Which statement is true?
it.h: Numbers farther to the left on the number line are less.

it.q: A bank account balance is -$25. How many dollars must be deposited to bring the balance to $0?
it.h: How far is -25 from 0?

it.q: A hawk flies 40 feet above sea level and a fish swims 15 feet below sea level, directly below the hawk. How many feet apart are they?
it.h: Add the distance of each from sea level.

it.q: Which list orders these elevations from lowest to highest: 12 m, -8 m, 0 m, -15 m?
it.h: Picture each elevation on a vertical number line.

it.q: Explain what abs(-20) = 20 means for a bank balance of -20 dollars.
it.ans: A balance of -20 means the account is 20 dollars below zero, a debt. The absolute value, 20, tells the size of the debt: the person owes 20 dollars.

lessons.u: Module 4: Expressions and equations
lessons.n: Exponents and the order of operations

it.h: 4^3 means 4 x 4 x 4.
Multiply before you subtract.
Evaluate the exponent first, then divide, then add.

it.q: Which expression equals 5 x 5 x 5 x 5?
Explain why 2^3 is not equal to 6.
it.ans: 2^3 means 2 x 2 x 2 = 8. An exponent shows repeated multiplication of the base, not the base times the exponent.

lessons.u: Module 4: Expressions and equations
lessons.n: Writing and evaluating expressions

it.q: Which expression means "7 more than a number n"?
it.h: "More than" means add.

it.q: Which expression means "the quotient of a number x and 4, decreased by 2"?
it.h: Write the quotient first, then show "decreased by 2".

it.q: Evaluate 5m - 3 when m = 6.
Evaluate 2a^2 + b when a = 3 and b = 4.
it.h: Find a^2 first, then multiply by 2, then add b.

it.q: Tickets cost $9 each, and there is one $4 service fee for the whole order. Which expression gives the cost of t tickets?
The expression 3x gives the cost in dollars of x pounds of apples. Explain what the 3 and the x mean.
it.ans: x is the number of pounds bought and 3 is the price per pound in dollars. Multiplying them gives the total cost.

lessons.u: Module 4: Expressions and equations
lessons.n: Equivalent expressions

it.q: Which expression is equivalent to 4(x + 3)?
it.h: Multiply 4 by each term inside the parentheses.

it.q: Which expression is equivalent to 5y + 2y + 3?
it.h: Only like terms can be combined.

it.q: Simplify 6a + 4 - 2a + 9. What is the coefficient of a?
it.h: Combine the a terms, then combine the numbers.

it.q: Which shows 18x + 12 written as a product using the GCF?
Which pair of expressions are equivalent?
Explain how you can test whether 3(x + 2) and 3x + 2 are equivalent.
it.ans: Substitute a value such as x = 1: 3(1 + 2) = 9 but 3(1) + 2 = 5. The values are different, so the expressions are not equivalent.

lessons.u: Module 4: Expressions and equations
lessons.n: Solving one-step equations

it.q: Solve x + 9 = 23.
it.h: What can you subtract from both sides to get x alone?

it.q: Solve 7y = 56.
Solve m ÷ 4 = 12.
it.h: Multiply both sides by 4.

it.q: Which value of n makes 3.5 + n = 10 true?
Solve 2/3 w = 10.
it.h: Multiply both sides by the reciprocal of 2/3.

it.q: Write and solve an equation: Lena has some stickers. After she gets 15 more, she has 42. How many did she start with?
it.ans: s + 15 = 42, so s = 42 - 15 = 27 stickers.

lessons.u: Module 4: Expressions and equations
lessons.n: Inequalities and relationships between two variables

it.q: Which inequality means "x is at least 18"?
it.h: "At least 18" includes 18.

it.q: Which number is a solution of x < 4.5?
A taxi ride costs c = 2m + 3 dollars for m miles. What is c when m = 8?
it.h: Replace m with 8.

it.q: In c = 2m + 3, which is the independent variable?
it.h: The independent variable is the one you choose; the other depends on it.

it.q: A ride requires riders to be taller than 48 inches. Which inequality shows the allowed heights h?
Explain the difference between the graphs of x > 3 and x >= 3 on a number line.
it.ans: Both are shaded to the right of 3. x > 3 uses an open circle at 3 because 3 is not a solution; x >= 3 uses a closed circle because 3 is a solution.

lessons.u: Module 4: Expressions and equations
lessons.n: Writing and solving equations from word problems

it.q: Jada has some stickers. After she gets 15 more, she has 52. Which equation fits?
it.h: She starts with s stickers and adds 15.

it.q: Seven friends share the cost of a pizza equally, and each pays $3.50. The equation p / 7 = 3.50 gives the price p. What is the price of the pizza, in dollars?
it.h: Multiply to undo dividing by 7.

it.q: A movie ticket costs $9. Lena spent $63 on tickets. How many tickets did she buy?
it.h: Write and solve 9t = 63.

it.q: The temperature rose 12 degrees to 71 degrees F. Which equation finds the starting temperature t?
it.h: The start plus the rise equals the end.

it.q: A rectangle has an area of 84 square feet and a width of 7 feet. What is its perimeter, in feet?
it.h: First solve 7L = 84 to find the length.

it.q: Write a word problem for the equation 4x = 28 and solve it.
it.ans: Example: 4 friends each buy the same number of trading cards, 28 cards in all. How many does each buy? x = 28 / 4 = 7 cards.

lessons.u: Module 4: Expressions and equations
lessons.n: Dependent and independent variables in tables, graphs and equations

it.q: A plumber charges $50 per hour. Which quantity is the independent variable?
it.h: Which quantity causes the other to change?

it.q: The equation c = 4p gives the cost c in dollars of p pounds of bananas. What is c when p = 6?
it.h: Replace p with 6.

it.q: A table shows x: 2, 3, 4, 5 and y: 18, 27, 36, 45. Which equation fits the table?
it.h: How does each y compare with its x?

it.q: A candle is 20 cm tall and burns 2 cm each hour. Its height after h hours is t = 20 - 2h. How tall is it after 6 hours, in cm?
it.h: Find 2 x 6 first.

it.q: A taxi charges $3 plus $2 per mile, so the cost is c = 2m + 3. A ride costs $19. How many miles long was the ride?
it.h: Try values of m, or work backward.

it.q: A graph shows hours studied on the x-axis and test score on the y-axis. Explain which is the dependent variable and why.
it.ans: The test score is the dependent variable because it depends on, or changes with, the number of hours studied. Hours studied is the independent variable.

lessons.u: Module 5: Area, surface area and volume problems
lessons.n: Area of triangles, parallelograms and trapezoids

it.q: A parallelogram has a base of 12 inches and a height of 7 inches. What is its area in square inches?
it.h: The area of a parallelogram is base times height.

it.q: A triangle has a base of 10 meters and a height of 9 meters. What is its area in square meters?
it.h: A triangle is half of a parallelogram with the same base and height.

it.q: A trapezoid has bases of 8 cm and 14 cm and a height of 5 cm. What is its area in square cm?
it.h: Add the two bases, multiply by the height, then take half.

it.q: A right triangle has legs of 6 feet and 11 feet and a longest side of about 12.5 feet. Which two lengths do you use to find its area?
it.h: The base and height must be perpendicular.

it.q: A triangular sail has a base of 3.5 meters and a height of 6 meters. What is its area in square meters?
Explain why the area of a triangle is 1/2 x base x height.
it.ans: Two copies of the same triangle fit together to make a parallelogram with the same base and height. The parallelogram's area is base x height, so one triangle has half of that area.

lessons.u: Module 5: Area, surface area and volume problems
lessons.n: Composite figures and polygons on the coordinate plane

it.q: An L-shaped room is made of a 10 ft by 8 ft rectangle and a 4 ft by 3 ft rectangle. What is its total area in square feet?
it.h: Find the area of each rectangle and add.

it.q: A triangle has vertices (1, 1), (7, 1) and (3, 5). What is its area in square units?
it.h: Use the horizontal side as the base. How far is the third vertex from that side?

it.q: A rectangle has vertices (-2, 3), (4, 3), (4, -1) and (-2, -1). What are its side lengths?
What is the perimeter in units of the rectangle with vertices (-2, 3), (4, 3), (4, -1) and (-2, -1)?
it.h: Find the length and width, then add all four sides.

it.q: A pentagon is split into a rectangle and a triangle. How do you find the pentagon's area?
ch: Add the area of the rectangle and the area of the triangle
Subtract the triangle's area from the rectangle's area

it.q: Describe two ways to find the area of a 10 by 10 square with a 4 by 4 square cut out of one corner.
it.ans: Subtract: 100 - 16 = 84 square units. Or split what is left into two rectangles, 10 x 6 = 60 and 6 x 4 = 24, and add: 84 square units.

lessons.u: Module 5: Area, surface area and volume problems
lessons.n: Volume of right rectangular prisms

it.q: A box is 6 cm long, 4 cm wide and 5 cm tall. What is its volume in cubic cm?
it.h: Multiply length x width x height.

it.q: A prism measures 2 1/2 inches by 2 inches by 4 inches. What is its volume in cubic inches?
How many cubes with 1/2-inch edges fill a box that is 2 inches by 1 inch by 1 inch?
it.h: How many half-inch cubes fit along each edge?

it.q: A rectangular prism has a base area of 18 square feet and a height of 2.5 feet. What is its volume?
it.h: Volume = area of the base x height.

it.q: A fish tank is 30 inches long, 12 inches wide and 16 inches tall. What is its volume in cubic inches?
Explain why packing a prism with 1/2-unit cubes and multiplying length x width x height give the same volume.
it.ans: Each 1/2-unit cube has a volume of 1/8 cubic unit. Counting the cubes and multiplying by 1/8 gives the same number as multiplying the three fractional edge lengths.

lessons.u: Module 5: Area, surface area and volume problems
lessons.n: Nets and surface area

it.q: How many faces does a rectangular prism have?
What is the surface area of a cube with edges of 4 cm, in square cm?
it.h: A cube has 6 congruent square faces.

it.q: A box is 5 inches by 3 inches by 2 inches. What is its surface area in square inches?
it.h: Find the area of each pair of matching faces.

it.q: A net has 1 square and 4 triangles. Which solid does it fold into?
Which situation needs surface area, not volume?
ch: wrapping paper to cover a gift box

it.q: Explain how a net helps you find the surface area of a prism.
