it.ans: A net unfolds the prism into its flat faces. Find the area of each face and add them to get the total area of the outside.

lessons.u: Module 5: Area, surface area and volume problems
lessons.n: Surface area and volume word problems: packaging and painting

it.q: A gift box is 8 inches long, 5 inches wide and 3 inches tall. How many square inches of wrapping paper cover it exactly, with no overlap?
it.h: Find the area of each pair of matching faces and add.

it.q: A cube-shaped toy box has edges of 1 1/2 feet. What is its volume in cubic feet?
it.h: Multiply 3/2 x 3/2 x 3/2.

it.q: Which measurement tells how much paint is needed to cover the outside of a closed box?
it.h: Paint covers the faces, which are flat areas.

it.q: A cereal box holds 240 cubic inches. Its base is 8 inches by 2 inches. How tall is it in inches?
it.h: Volume equals the area of the base times the height.

it.q: A storage cube has edges of 4 feet. One quart of paint covers 40 square feet. How many quarts are needed to paint all 6 faces?
it.h: Find the surface area first.

it.q: Explain why surface area is measured in square units but volume is measured in cubic units.
it.ans: Surface area counts the flat squares that cover the faces, so it uses two dimensions. Volume counts the cubes that fill the space inside, so it uses three dimensions.

lessons.u: Module 5: Area, surface area and volume problems
lessons.n: Volume with fractional edge lengths and unit cubes

it.q: How many cubes with 1/2-inch edges fill a box 2 inches long, 1 inch wide and 1 inch tall?
it.h: How many 1/2-inch cubes fit along each edge?

it.q: A box is 1/2 foot by 3/4 foot by 2 feet. What is its volume in cubic feet?
it.h: Multiply all three edge lengths.

it.q: What is the volume of one cube with an edge of 1/3 yard?
it.h: Multiply 1/3 by itself three times.

it.q: A prism is 4 1/2 cm long, 2 cm wide and 3 cm tall. What is its volume in cubic cm?
it.h: Multiply in an order that is easy, such as 4 1/2 x 2 first.

it.q: Cube-shaped candies with 1/4-inch edges are packed into a box 2 inches long, 1 inch wide and 1/2 inch tall. How many candies fill the box?
it.h: Count how many candies fit along each edge.

it.q: Explain why packing a box that is 3/2 by 1 by 1 units with cubes of edge 1/2 unit gives the same volume as V = l x w x h.
it.ans: 3, 2 and 2 half-unit cubes fit along the edges, so 12 cubes fill the box. Each cube has a volume of 1/8, so 12 x 1/8 = 1 1/2 cubic units. Also 3/2 x 1 x 1 = 1 1/2. Both ways give the same volume.

lessons.u: Module 6: Statistics
lessons.n: Statistical questions and data displays

it.q: Which is a statistical question?
ch: How many hours do students in our class sleep on school nights?
How many hours did I sleep last night?
How many days are in a week?
it.h: A statistical question expects answers that vary.

it.q: A dot plot of shoe sizes has 3 dots at 6, 5 dots at 7, 2 dots at 8 and 1 dot at 10. How many students were surveyed?
it.h: Each dot is one student.

it.q: A dot plot shows 3 dots at size 6, 5 dots at size 7, 2 dots at size 8 and 1 dot at size 10. How many students wear size 8 or larger?
A histogram has bars for 0-9, 10-19, 20-29 and 30-39 minutes of reading. Which question can it answer?
ch: How many students read 20 to 29 minutes?
Exactly how many minutes did each student read?

it.q: Most values in a data set are low, and a few are much higher. How is the shape described?
it.h: A distribution is skewed toward the side of its long tail.

it.q: Change the question "How tall am I?" into a statistical question, and explain why yours is statistical.
it.ans: "How tall are the students in my class?" It is statistical because the answers vary from student to student.

lessons.u: Module 6: Statistics
lessons.n: Mean and mean absolute deviation

it.q: What is the mean of 6, 9, 10, 4 and 11?
it.h: Add the values and divide by how many there are.

it.q: The mean of four test scores is 85. Three of the scores are 80, 90 and 78. What is the fourth score?
it.h: The four scores must add up to 4 x 85.

it.q: Find the mean absolute deviation (MAD) of 2, 4, 6, 8 and 10.
it.h: Find the mean, find how far each value is from the mean, then find the mean of those distances.

it.q: Two classes both have a mean of 20 minutes of reading. Class A has a MAD of 2 minutes and Class B has a MAD of 9 minutes. What does this tell you?
ch: Class B's reading times are more spread out
Both classes have the same spread

it.q: Five friends have 3, 5, 5, 8 and 9 dollars. If they share the money equally, how many dollars does each friend get?
Explain what the mean represents, using the idea of a fair share.
it.ans: The mean is the amount each value would be if the total were shared equally among all the values.

lessons.u: Module 6: Statistics
lessons.n: Median, interquartile range and box plots

it.q: What is the median of 14, 9, 21, 6 and 17?
it.h: Put the values in order first.

it.q: What is the median of 3, 8, 10, 15, 20, 22?
it.h: With an even number of values, find the mean of the two middle values.

it.q: What is the interquartile range (IQR) of 2, 4, 5, 7, 8, 10, 12, 15?
it.h: Find the median of the lower half and of the upper half, then subtract.

it.q: A box plot has a minimum of 10, Q1 of 15, median of 20, Q3 of 30 and maximum of 45. What is the range?
A box plot has Q1 = 15 and Q3 = 30. About what fraction of the data lies between 15 and 30?
it.h: The box covers the middle part of the data.

it.q: Explain what the five-number summary tells you about a data set.
it.ans: The minimum and maximum show the extremes, Q1 and Q3 mark the edges of the middle half of the data, and the median is the middle value.

lessons.u: Module 6: Statistics
lessons.n: Describing distributions and choosing measures

it.q: Most home prices on a street are near $500,000, but one is $3,000,000. Which measure of center best describes a typical home?
it.h: Which measure is affected less by one very large value?

it.q: A data set is roughly symmetric with no outliers. Which pair of measures should you use to describe it?
Quiz scores are 6, 7, 7, 8, 9, 10 and 2. What is the median score?
it.h: Order the scores first.

it.q: Scores are 10, 12, 13, 15 and 50. How much greater is the mean than the median?
it.h: Find each measure, then subtract.

it.q: A store records the number of customers each hour. Which statement uses the median of 32 customers correctly?
ch: Half of the hours had 32 or fewer customers
The store had 32 customers in all

it.q: Explain how an outlier affects the mean and the median differently.
it.ans: An outlier pulls the mean toward it because every value is added into the total. The median depends only on the middle position, so it changes little or not at all.

lessons.u: Module 6: Statistics
lessons.n: Histograms and frequency tables

it.q: A frequency table of test scores shows 60-69: 3 students, 70-79: 7 students, 80-89: 9 students and 90-99: 5 students. How many students are in the data set?
it.h: Add the frequencies.

it.q: A histogram shows the heights of plants in the intervals 0-4 cm, 5-9 cm, 10-14 cm and 15-19 cm. Which question can the histogram answer?
ch: How many plants were from 10 to 14 cm tall?
What was the exact height of the tallest plant?
What is the mean height to the nearest tenth?
it.h: A histogram shows how many values fall in each interval, not each exact value.

it.q: A frequency table of minutes spent reading shows 0-14: 2 students, 15-29: 6 students, 30-44: 10 students and 45-59: 2 students. How many students read at least 30 minutes?
it.h: Which intervals have values of 30 or more?

it.q: The ages of 10 people at a park are 12, 15, 21, 23, 27, 28, 29, 34, 36 and 38. Using the intervals 10-19, 20-29 and 30-39, which interval has the greatest frequency?
ch: They all have the same frequency
it.h: Tally each age into an interval.

it.q: A frequency table of hours of sleep shows 6-6.9: 4 students, 7-7.9: 8 students, 8-8.9: 6 students and 9-9.9: 2 students. What percent of the students slept at least 8 hours?
it.h: Find the total number of students first.

it.q: Explain why a histogram cannot be used to find the exact median of a data set.
it.ans: A histogram only shows how many values fall in each interval. You can tell which interval holds the median, but not its exact value, because the individual numbers are not shown.

lessons.u: Module 6: Statistics
lessons.n: Comparing two groups with dot plots and box plots

it.q: Class A's quiz scores are 6, 7, 7, 8, 9, 10 and 10. What is the median score?
it.h: The median is the middle value when the data are in order.

it.q: A box plot of plant heights has a minimum of 4 cm, Q1 of 7 cm, a median of 9 cm, Q3 of 12 cm and a maximum of 15 cm. What is the interquartile range, in cm?
it.h: Subtract Q1 from Q3.

it.q: Box plot X has a median of 20 and an IQR of 4. Box plot Y has a median of 20 and an IQR of 12. Which statement is true?
ch: The middle half of Y is more spread out
The middle half of X is more spread out
it.h: The IQR measures the spread of the middle half of the data.

it.q: A dot plot of the number of siblings shows 0 (3 dots), 1 (5 dots), 2 (4 dots), 3 (2 dots) and 4 (1 dot). How many students have at least 2 siblings?
it.h: Count the dots at 2, 3 and 4.

it.q: Team Red's heights in inches are 58, 60, 61, 63 and 63. Team Blue's heights are 55, 59, 62, 64 and 70. How many inches greater is Blue's range than Red's range?
it.h: Range = maximum - minimum.

it.q: Explain what you can learn by comparing the medians and the IQRs of two box plots.
it.ans: The medians tell which group has a greater typical value. The IQRs tell which group's middle half is more spread out, so you can see which group is more consistent.

lessons.u: Module 1: Ratios and proportional relationships
lessons.n: Proportional relationships in tables

it.q: Which table shows a proportional relationship?
it.h: Check whether y ÷ x is the same for every pair.

it.q: In a proportional relationship, y = 18 when x = 4. What is y when x = 10?
it.h: Find y when x = 1 first.

it.q: A climbing gym charges $10 per class plus a one-time $20 card fee. Is the total cost proportional to the number of classes?
ch: No, because 0 classes would still cost $20
Yes, because the cost goes up by $10 each time
No, because the cost goes up by the same amount each time

it.q: Trail mix is sold by weight. 3 pounds cost $13.50. How many dollars do 7 pounds cost?
it.h: Find the price of 1 pound.

it.q: Explain how to decide from a table whether two quantities are proportional.
it.ans: Divide each y-value by its x-value. If every quotient is the same number, the quantities are proportional and that number is the constant of proportionality.

lessons.u: Module 1: Ratios and proportional relationships
lessons.n: Graphs, equations and the constant of proportionality

it.q: In y = 3.5x, what is the constant of proportionality?
it.h: In y = kx, the constant is k.

it.q: Which graph shows a proportional relationship?
it.h: Think about what happens to y when x is 0.

it.q: The graph of a proportional relationship passes through (4, 10). What is the constant of proportionality?
it.h: Divide y by x.

it.q: A recipe uses 3 cups of flour for every 2 eggs. Which equation gives the cups of flour f for e eggs?
The point (1, r) is on the graph of y = 6x. What is r?
A graph of distance in miles against time in hours passes through (0, 0) and (3, 180). Explain what the point (1, 60) means.
it.ans: After 1 hour the car has traveled 60 miles. 60 miles per hour is the unit rate, which is the constant of proportionality.

lessons.u: Module 1: Ratios and proportional relationships
lessons.n: Ratios and rates involving fractions

it.q: Pat walks 1/2 mile in 1/4 hour. What is her speed in miles per hour?
it.h: Divide the distance by the time.

it.q: A recipe uses 3/4 cup of sugar for 1/2 of a batch. How many cups of sugar are needed for a full batch?
A pump fills 2/3 of a tank in 1/2 hour. How many tanks does it fill per hour?
it.h: Find the amount for 1 hour: 2/3 ÷ 1/2.

it.q: What is the unit rate for 1 1/4 miles in 1/2 hour?
A snail crawls 5/6 foot in 2/3 minute. How many feet per minute is that?
Explain how to find the unit rate when 3/4 can of paint covers 1/2 of a wall, and what the unit rate means.
it.ans: Divide 3/4 by 1/2 to get 1 1/2 cans per wall. It means one whole wall needs 1 1/2 cans of paint.

lessons.u: Module 1: Ratios and proportional relationships
lessons.n: Ratios of scale drawings

it.q: A map scale is 1 cm : 5 km. Two towns are 7 cm apart on the map. How many kilometers apart are they?
it.h: Each centimeter on the map stands for 5 kilometers.

it.q: A blueprint uses 1 inch : 4 feet. A room is 15 feet long. How many inches long is it on the blueprint?
A scale drawing of a garden is 6 in by 4 in with a scale of 1 in : 3 ft. What is the actual area of the garden in square feet?
it.h: Find the actual length and width first.

it.q: A drawing is enlarged with a scale factor of 2. What happens to its area?
A model car is 1/24 the size of the real car. The model is 7.5 inches long. How many inches long is the real car?
Explain what a scale factor of 1/50 means for a scale drawing of a building.
it.ans: Every length on the drawing is 1/50 of the actual length, so 1 unit on the drawing represents 50 units on the building.

lessons.u: Module 1: Ratios and proportional relationships
lessons.n: Comparing proportional relationships and best buys

it.q: A 12-ounce bottle of shampoo costs $4.20. What is the price per ounce, in dollars?
it.h: Divide the cost by the number of ounces.

it.q: Which is the better buy?
ch: They cost the same per bar
it.h: Find the cost of one bar in each package.

it.q: Printer A prints 45 pages in 3 minutes. Printer B prints y = 18x pages in x minutes. How many more pages per minute does Printer B print?
it.h: Find the unit rate for Printer A.

it.q: Car A uses 12 gallons of gas to go 360 miles. Car B goes d = 28g miles on g gallons. Which car goes farther on one gallon?
ch: They go the same distance per gallon
it.h: Find miles per gallon for Car A.

it.q: Store X sells 3 pounds of grapes for $5.40. Store Y sells 5 pounds for $8.50. How many dollars are saved by buying 10 pounds at the cheaper store instead of the other store?
it.h: Find each price per pound, then multiply by 10.

it.q: Ava runs 3/4 mile in 6 minutes. Sam runs 1 1/2 miles in 15 minutes. Explain who runs faster.
it.ans: Ava: 3/4 / 6 = 1/8 mile per minute, or 0.125. Sam: 1.5 / 15 = 0.1 mile per minute. Ava runs farther each minute, so she is faster.

lessons.u: Module 1: Ratios and proportional relationships
lessons.n: Interpreting points on graphs of proportional relationships

it.q: A graph of a proportional relationship passes through (4, 30). What is the y-value of the point where x = 1?
it.h: The point (1, r) shows the unit rate.

it.q: A graph shows the cost in dollars (y) of x pounds of grapes and passes through (1, 2.5). What does this point mean?
ch: The store sells 2.5 kinds of grapes
Grapes are free for the first 2.5 pounds
it.h: The x-coordinate is pounds and the y-coordinate is dollars.

it.q: Which point must be on the graph of every proportional relationship?
it.h: What does 0 of one quantity give of the other?

it.q: The graph of y = kx passes through (6, 9). What is k?
it.h: k = y / x.

it.q: A line through the origin and (5, 40) shows the dollars earned for hours worked. How many dollars are earned in 7.5 hours?
it.h: Find the unit rate first.

it.q: Explain what the point (0, 0) means on a graph of the distance a cyclist rides over time.
it.ans: At 0 minutes the cyclist has ridden 0 distance. A proportional relationship always includes (0, 0), because none of one quantity matches none of the other.

lessons.u: Module 1: Ratios and proportional relationships
lessons.n: Deciding whether real-world relationships are proportional

it.q: Which relationship is proportional?
ch: the cost of apples at $1.20 per pound
a gym fee of $25 plus $10 per month
a parking fee of $5 plus $1.50 per hour
it.h: Is there a starting amount other than 0?

it.q: A table shows x: 2, 4, 6 and y: 5, 10, 15. Is the relationship proportional?
ch: No, because the y-values are odd
Yes, because the x-values are even
it.h: Find y/x for each pair.

it.q: A gym charges a $25 sign-up fee plus $10 per month. What is the total cost for 3 months, in dollars?
it.h: Add the fee to the monthly charges.

it.q: A table shows x: 1, 2, 3 and y: 4, 7, 10. Why is it not proportional?
ch: The ratios y/x are 4, 3.5 and about 3.33, which are not equal
The y-values are not all even
The x-values do not start at 0
it.h: Compare y/x for each pair.

it.q: Shop A charges $8 per T-shirt. Shop B charges $5 per T-shirt plus a $27 setup fee. For how many shirts do the two shops cost the same?
it.h: Write a cost expression for each shop and set them equal.

it.q: Explain why the total cost of a pizza order with a $4 delivery fee is not proportional to the number of pizzas.
it.ans: With the fee, the cost per pizza is not constant: doubling the number of pizzas does not double the cost. The graph would start at $4 instead of going through (0, 0).

lessons.u: Module 2: Rational numbers
lessons.n: Adding integers and rational numbers

it.h: Start at -8 on a number line and move 3 units to the right.
The signs are different, so subtract the absolute values and use the sign of the number farther from 0.

it.q: Which sum is 0?
it.h: Opposites are additive inverses.

it.q: A diver at -25 feet swims up 11 feet. What is her new position in feet?
Use a number line to explain why -3 + 5 = 2.
it.ans: Start at -3 and move 5 units to the right. The first 3 units bring you to 0 and 2 more units bring you to 2.

lessons.u: Module 2: Rational numbers
lessons.n: Subtracting rational numbers and distance

it.h: Subtracting a number is the same as adding its opposite.

it.q: Which expression equals 8 - (-3)?
What is the distance on a number line between -17 and 6?
it.h: The distance between p and q is abs(p - q).

it.q: Use a real-world situation to explain why 4 - (-6) = 10.
it.ans: If you have $4 and a $6 debt is taken away, you are $6 better off. Taking away -6 is the same as adding 6, so 4 - (-6) = 4 + 6 = 10.

lessons.u: Module 2: Rational numbers
lessons.n: Multiplying and dividing rational numbers

it.h: The product of two negative numbers is positive.

it.q: Which product is positive?
it.h: Count the negative factors.

it.q: Use a pattern to explain why -3 x -1 = 3.
it.ans: -3 x 2 = -6, -3 x 1 = -3 and -3 x 0 = 0. Each time the second factor goes down by 1, the product goes up by 3, so -3 x -1 = 3.

lessons.u: Module 2: Rational numbers
lessons.n: Rational numbers as decimals and multi-step problems

it.q: What is 5/8 as a decimal?
it.h: Divide 5 by 8.

it.q: Which fraction has a repeating decimal?
it.h: Divide each numerator by its denominator.
Multiply before adding.

it.q: A freezer is at 3 degrees. It cools 2.5 degrees each hour. What is its temperature after 4 hours, in degrees?
Explain how you know 1/6 is a repeating decimal.
it.ans: Dividing 1 by 6 gives 0.1666... The remainder 4 appears again and again, so the digit 6 repeats forever.

lessons.u: Module 2: Rational numbers
lessons.n: Real-world problems with positive and negative rational numbers

it.q: The temperature was -3.5 degrees C at midnight and dropped 2.25 degrees by 4 a.m. What was the temperature at 4 a.m., in degrees C?
it.h: A drop means adding a negative number.

it.q: A diver at -18 meters rises 7.5 meters. What is her new elevation, in meters?
it.h: Rising means adding a positive number.

it.q: A stock lost $1.40 in value each day for 5 days. Which expression gives the total change in its value?
it.h: The same loss repeats 5 times.

it.q: Ravi's account balance was -$32.50. He deposits $50 and then pays a $12.75 fee. What is the new balance, in dollars?
it.h: Work from left to right, one change at a time.

it.q: Over 4 hours the temperature changed by -10 degrees in all. In the fifth hour it rose 3 degrees. What was the mean change per hour over all 5 hours?
it.h: Find the total change for the 5 hours, then divide.

it.q: Explain why the expression 20 - (-8) tells how many feet a bird at 20 feet above sea level is above a fish at -8 feet.
it.ans: Subtracting finds the distance between two elevations. Subtracting -8 is the same as adding 8, so 20 - (-8) = 28 feet: 20 feet above sea level plus 8 feet below it.

lessons.u: Module 2: Rational numbers
lessons.n: Properties of operations with rational numbers

it.q: Use properties of operations to find -25 x 7 x 4 mentally.
it.h: Multiply -25 x 4 first.
Look for opposites that add to 0.

it.q: Which property shows that -2(5 - 3) = -10 + 6?
it.h: The -2 multiplies each term inside the parentheses.
Use the commutative property to group numbers that are easy to multiply.

it.q: What is the sign of the product of five negative numbers and two positive numbers?
it.h: Each pair of negative factors makes a positive product.

it.q: Explain how to use the distributive property to find -4 x 2.25 mentally.

lessons.u: Module 3: Expressions and equations
lessons.n: Writing equivalent expressions

it.q: Expand 4(2x - 3).
it.h: Multiply 4 by each term in the parentheses.

it.q: Which expression is equivalent to 5x - 2(x + 4)?
it.h: Distribute -2 to both terms in the parentheses.

it.q: Simplify 3.5y - 1.2y + 4. What is the coefficient of y?
Which is a factored form of 12a - 18?
it.h: Find the greatest common factor of 12 and 18.

it.q: A price p is increased by 15%. Which expression is equivalent to p + 0.15p?
Explain why 1.15p and p + 0.15p are equivalent, and what each shows about a price.
it.ans: p + 0.15p = 1p + 0.15p = 1.15p by combining like terms. p + 0.15p shows the price plus the increase; 1.15p shows the new price is 115% of the original.

lessons.u: Module 3: Expressions and equations
lessons.n: Solving equations

it.q: Solve 3x + 5 = 26.
it.h: Undo the addition first, then the multiplication.

it.q: Solve -2x - 7 = 9.
Solve 4(x + 3) = 36.
it.h: Divide both sides by 4 first, or distribute.

it.q: Solve 1/2 x + 6 = 15.
A rectangle's perimeter is 50 cm and its length is 15 cm. Which equation finds its width w?
Write and solve an equation: A phone case costs $8 more than twice the cost of a screen protector. The case costs $26. How much is the screen protector?
it.ans: 2p + 8 = 26, so 2p = 18 and p = 9. The screen protector costs $9.

lessons.u: Module 3: Expressions and equations
lessons.n: Solving inequalities

it.q: Which inequality matches "at most 12"?
it.h: "At most" means the value can be 12 or less.

it.q: Solve 2x - 3 > 11.
it.h: Solve it like an equation, then check the direction of the sign.

it.q: Solve -3x <= 12.
it.h: When you divide by a negative number, reverse the inequality sign.

it.q: Movie tickets cost $9 each and parking costs $12. Ines has $80. What is the greatest number of tickets she can buy?
Which value is a solution of 5 - x > 2?
Explain why the inequality sign reverses when you multiply or divide both sides by a negative number.
it.ans: Multiplying by a negative number flips numbers to the other side of 0, which reverses their order. For example, 2 < 5, but -2 > -5.

lessons.u: Module 3: Expressions and equations
lessons.n: Circumference and area of circles

it.q: What is the circumference of a circle with a diameter of 10 cm? Use 3.14 for pi.
it.h: C = pi x d.

it.q: What is the area of a circle with a radius of 3 m? Use 3.14 for pi.
it.h: A = pi x r^2.

it.q: A circle has a circumference of 18.84 inches. What is its diameter in inches? Use 3.14 for pi.
The radius of a circle is doubled. What happens to its circumference?
What is the area of a semicircle with a diameter of 8 feet, in square feet? Use 3.14 for pi.
it.h: Find the radius, find the area of the whole circle, then take half.

it.q: Explain the relationship between the circumference and the diameter of any circle.
it.ans: For every circle, the circumference divided by the diameter is the same number, pi, about 3.14. So C = pi x d.

lessons.u: Module 3: Expressions and equations
lessons.n: Equations of the form p(x + q) = r in real-world problems

it.q: Solve 3(x + 4) = 27.
it.h: Divide both sides by 3 first.
Divide both sides by -2 and watch the signs.

it.q: Four friends each buy a ticket and a $3 snack. They spend $56 in all. Which equation finds the ticket price t?
it.h: Each friend's cost is t + 3.

it.q: A rectangular garden has a perimeter of 54 feet and a length of 15 feet. What is its width, in feet?
it.h: The perimeter is 2 times the sum of the length and the width.
Multiply both sides by 2.

it.q: Solve 5(x - 2) = 35 two different ways and explain each.
it.ans: Way 1: divide both sides by 5 to get x - 2 = 7, then add 2: x = 9. Way 2: distribute to get 5x - 10 = 35, add 10 to get 5x = 45, then divide by 5: x = 9.

lessons.u: Module 3: Expressions and equations
lessons.n: Two-step inequalities in budgets and limits

it.q: Solve 3x + 5 < 20. What is the greatest whole number that makes it true?
it.h: Subtract 5 from both sides, then divide by 3.

it.q: Sam has $40. He pays a $10 entry fee at a fair and wants rides that cost $3 each. Which inequality finds the number of rides r he can afford?
it.h: The total he spends must be at most 40.

it.q: Solve -2x + 7 >= 1. What is the greatest value of x?
it.h: When you divide by a negative number, reverse the inequality sign.

it.q: A van can carry at most 1,200 pounds. The driver weighs 180 pounds and each box weighs 40 pounds. What is the greatest number of boxes the van can carry along with the driver?
Which number is a solution of 4x - 3 > 9?
it.h: Solve the inequality, then check each choice.

it.q: Explain why the inequality sign is reversed when you solve -3x > 12.
it.ans: Dividing both sides by -3 gives x < -4. Multiplying or dividing by a negative number reverses the order of numbers: 2 < 5, but -2 > -5. So the sign must be reversed to keep the statement true.

lessons.u: Module 3: Expressions and equations
lessons.n: Rewriting expressions to show meaning in context

it.q: A price p is increased by 6%. Which expression shows the new price?
it.h: The new price is all of p plus 6% of p.

it.q: Which expression is equivalent to a + 0.2a?
it.h: Think of a as 1a.

it.q: Simplify 3(2x + 5) - 4x. What is the constant term?
it.h: Distribute first, then combine like terms.

it.q: A shirt costs d dollars and is on sale for 25% off. Which two expressions both show the sale price?
it.h: Taking away 25% leaves 75%.

it.q: A rectangle's length is 3 more than its width w, so its perimeter is 2(w + 3 + w), which simplifies to 4w + 6. What is the perimeter when w = 8?
it.h: Substitute 8 for w.

it.q: Explain why the expressions 0.8x and x - 0.2x both describe a price after a 20% discount.
it.ans: x - 0.2x subtracts 20% of the price from the price. Combining like terms gives 1x - 0.2x = 0.8x, which means you pay 80% of the price. The expressions are equivalent.

lessons.u: Module 4: Percent and proportional relationships
lessons.n: Percent of a quantity and finding the whole

it.q: What is 35% of 240?
it.h: Write 35% as 0.35 and multiply.

it.q: 18 is 24% of what number?
it.h: Write the equation 0.24n = 18.

it.q: What percent of 80 is 52?
Which expression is the same as 125% of a number n?
A school has 640 students and 15% of them are in the band. How many students are in the band?
Explain how to find 0.5% of 600.
it.ans: 0.5% = 0.005, and 0.005 x 600 = 3. Or 1% of 600 is 6, and 0.5% is half of that, 3.

lessons.u: Module 4: Percent and proportional relationships
lessons.n: Percent increase, decrease and error

it.q: A town grew from 2,000 to 2,500 people. What is the percent increase?
it.h: Find the amount of change, then divide by the original amount.

it.q: A price dropped from $80 to $68. What is the percent decrease?
A $50 item increases in price by 20% and then decreases by 20%. What is the final price?
it.h: The second percent is taken of the new price.

it.q: Ana estimated there were 45 beans in a jar. There were actually 50. What is her percent error?
it.h: Percent error = abs(estimate - actual) ÷ actual x 100.

it.q: Which expression gives the new value after a 12% decrease from x?
Explain why a 10% increase followed by a 10% decrease does not return to the original amount.
it.ans: The decrease is 10% of a larger number. For example, 100 increases to 110, and then 10% of 110 is 11, so it decreases to 99.

lessons.u: Module 4: Percent and proportional relationships
lessons.n: Markups, discounts, tax, tips, commission and interest

it.q: A $60 jacket is on sale for 30% off. What is the sale price in dollars?
it.h: With 30% off, you pay 70% of the price.

it.q: A meal costs $40 and the tip is 18%. What is the total in dollars?
A store buys a lamp for $25 and marks it up 80%. What is the selling price in dollars?
Sales tax is 8.5%. Which expression gives the total cost of an item priced at p dollars?
A salesperson earns a 6% commission. How many dollars of commission does she earn on a $3,500 sale?
Show two ways to find the price of a $35 item after a 20% discount.
it.ans: Find 20% of 35, which is 7, and subtract: 35 - 7 = $28. Or find 80% of 35: 0.8 x 35 = $28.

lessons.u: Module 4: Percent and proportional relationships
lessons.n: Percent in scale drawings and mixtures

it.q: A drawing is reduced to 60% of its original size. A line on it was 15 cm long. How long is the line now, in cm?
it.h: Multiply the length by 0.60.

it.q: A photo is enlarged to 150% of its size. Its width was 8 inches. What is its new width in inches?
A scale drawing uses 1 cm to represent 4 m. The drawing's lengths are what percent of the actual lengths?
it.h: 4 m is 400 cm.

it.q: A 20-liter mixture is 30% juice. How many liters of juice does it contain?
A bag of 50 marbles is 20% blue. How many blue marbles are in the bag?
Explain what it means if a scale drawing is 200% of the original figure.
it.ans: Every length in the drawing is 2 times the matching length in the original, so the drawing is an enlargement.

lessons.u: Module 4: Percent and proportional relationships
lessons.n: Finding the original amount before a percent change

it.q: After a 20% discount, a jacket costs $48. What was the original price, in dollars?
it.h: The sale price is 80% of the original price.

it.q: A town's population grew 10% to 5,500 people. What was the population before the growth?
it.h: The new population is 110% of the old population.

it.q: A store sells a bike for $180 after a 25% markup on its cost. Which equation finds the store's cost c?
it.h: A 25% markup means the price is 100% + 25% of the cost.

it.q: Jon spent 30% of his savings on a game that cost $42. How many dollars did he have in savings?
it.h: 30% of what number is 42?

it.q: A meal's total with a 15% tip was $34.50. What was the cost of the meal before the tip, in dollars?
it.h: The total is 115% of the meal's cost.

it.q: Tara says a shirt that costs $40 after a 20% discount originally cost $48, because 20% of 40 is 8. Explain her mistake and find the original price.
it.ans: The 20% discount was taken from the original price, not from $40. $40 is 80% of the original, so the original is 40 / 0.8 = $50. Check: 20% of 50 is 10, and 50 - 10 = 40.

lessons.u: Module 4: Percent and proportional relationships
lessons.n: Percent in survey data and circle graphs

it.q: In a survey of 80 students, 28 chose basketball as their favorite sport. What percent chose basketball?
it.h: Divide the part by the whole, then write it as a percent.

it.q: A circle graph shows that 25% of a family's $2,400 monthly budget is for rent. How many dollars go to rent?
it.h: 25% is one fourth.

it.q: In a circle graph, what central angle does a section showing 20% of the data have?
it.h: A full circle is 360 degrees.

it.q: A survey of 250 people found that 46% prefer cats, 38% prefer dogs and the rest prefer neither. How many people prefer neither?
it.h: First find the percent who prefer neither.

it.q: In a class of 30 students, 12 are in the band. Which is NOT equal to the part of the class in the band?
it.h: Write 12/30 in simplest form.

it.q: Explain how you know that the percents in a circle graph should add to 100%.
it.ans: The whole circle stands for all of the data. Each section is part of the whole, so all of the parts together make the whole, which is 100%.

lessons.u: Module 5: Statistics and probability
lessons.n: Probability and probability models

it.q: A bag has 3 red, 5 blue and 2 green marbles. One marble is drawn at random. What is P(blue)?
it.h: Probability = number of favorable outcomes ÷ total number of outcomes.

it.q: An event has a probability of 0.95. How likely is it?
A spinner has 8 equal sections numbered 1 to 8. What is the probability of spinning a number greater than 5?
Which probability model is uniform?
ch: a spinner that is 1/2 red, 1/4 blue and 1/4 green
a bag with 4 red tiles and 1 blue tile
it.h: In a uniform model every outcome has the same probability.

it.q: A letter is chosen at random from the word CALIFORNIA. What is the probability that it is an A?
Explain why the probability of an event must be between 0 and 1.
it.ans: A probability compares the favorable outcomes to all outcomes. The favorable outcomes can range from none (0) to all of them (1), never fewer than none or more than all.

lessons.u: Module 5: Statistics and probability
lessons.n: Experimental probability and simulation

it.q: A spinner landed on red 18 times in 60 spins. What is the experimental probability of red?
it.h: Divide the number of reds by the total number of spins.

it.q: A coin landed heads 27 times in 50 flips. What is the experimental probability of heads, as a decimal?
A spinner landed on red in 18 of 60 spins. Based on this, how many reds would you predict in 200 spins?
Why might an experimental probability be different from the theoretical probability?
ch: Random results vary, especially in a small number of trials

it.q: A factory finds 6 defective light bulbs in a sample of 400. How many defective bulbs would it predict in a batch of 5,000?
it.h: Find the fraction that were defective, then multiply.

it.q: Describe a simulation with a number cube to estimate the probability that a player who makes 1/3 of her shots makes at least 2 of her next 3 shots.
it.ans: Let 1 and 2 stand for a made shot and 3 to 6 for a miss. Roll the cube 3 times for one trial and record whether there are at least 2 makes. Repeat for many trials and divide the number of successes by the number of trials.

lessons.u: Module 5: Statistics and probability
lessons.n: Compound events

it.q: A coin is flipped twice. What is the probability of getting two heads?
it.h: List the outcomes: HH, HT, TH, TT.

it.q: A sandwich shop offers 3 kinds of bread and 4 fillings. How many different sandwiches with one bread and one filling are possible?
it.h: Use a tree diagram, or multiply.

it.q: A number cube is rolled and a coin is flipped. What is the probability of an even number and heads?
How many outcomes are in the sample space for rolling two number cubes?
Two number cubes are rolled. What is the probability that the sum is 7?
it.h: Make a 6 by 6 table of sums.

it.q: Describe how to use an organized list to find the sample space for flipping a coin three times.
it.ans: Choose H or T for the first flip, then each choice for the second and third flips: HHH, HHT, HTH, HTT, THH, THT, TTH, TTT. There are 8 outcomes.

lessons.u: Module 5: Statistics and probability
lessons.n: Random sampling and comparing populations

it.q: Which sample is most likely to represent all students at a school?
ch: 50 students chosen at random from the school roster
it.h: A random sample gives every member of the population the same chance of being chosen.

it.q: In a random sample of 60 students, 21 walk to school. The school has 900 students. About how many students walk to school?
Which survey question is biased?
ch: Don't you agree that our great park needs a new playground?
Do you think the park needs a new playground?
How often do you visit the park?
Which part of the park do you use most?

it.q: Class A's quiz scores have a mean of 82 and Class B's have a mean of 76. Both have a MAD of 4. How many MADs apart are the means?
it.h: Divide the difference of the means by the MAD.

it.q: Why do different random samples from the same population give different results?
ch: Each sample includes different individuals by chance
Only one sample can be correct

it.q: Explain why surveying people at a gym is not a good way to estimate how often people in a town exercise.
it.ans: People at a gym probably exercise more than most people in town, so the sample is biased and does not represent the whole town.

lessons.u: Module 5: Statistics and probability
lessons.n: Making predictions from samples and probabilities

it.q: In a random sample of 50 students at a school, 18 walk to school. The school has 600 students. About how many students in the school walk to school?
it.h: Find the fraction of the sample that walks, then use it for the whole school.

it.q: A fair number cube is rolled 120 times. About how many times should it land on 5?
it.h: The probability of rolling a 5 is 1/6.

it.q: A factory checks a random sample of 200 light bulbs and finds 4 defective. About how many defective bulbs would you expect in 5,000 bulbs?
it.h: What fraction of the sample is defective?

it.q: A spinner has 8 equal sections, and 3 of them are blue. If it is spun 400 times, about how many times should it land on blue?
it.h: Multiply the probability by the number of spins.

it.q: Which sample is most likely to give a good prediction of the favorite lunch of all students in a school?
ch: 60 students chosen at random from the whole school list
the 60 students in the pizza line
the 60 members of the soccer team
the first 60 students to arrive in the morning
it.h: A good sample gives every student the same chance to be chosen.

it.q: Two random samples of 40 voters in a town show 22 and 26 people supporting a new park. Explain what the samples suggest about the whole town.
it.ans: Both samples show more than half supporting the park (55% and 65%). Samples vary, but together they suggest that about 55% to 65% of the town supports the park, so a majority probably supports it.

lessons.u: Module 5: Statistics and probability
lessons.n: Comparing two populations with visual overlap and MAD

it.q: Two groups have means of 62 and 70. Each has a mean absolute deviation (MAD) of 4. How many MADs apart are the means?
it.h: Divide the difference in the means by the MAD.

it.q: The data 4, 6, 8, 10 and 12 have a mean of 8. What is the mean absolute deviation?
it.h: Find each value's distance from 8, then find the mean of those distances.

it.q: Two dot plots of plant heights have means of 30 cm and 31 cm, and each has a MAD of 6 cm. Which is the best description?
ch: The groups overlap a lot; the difference in means is small compared with the variability
The groups do not overlap at all
The second group is much taller
The groups have very different variability
it.h: Compare the difference in means with the MAD.

it.q: Group A has a median of 15 and an IQR of 4. Group B has a median of 23 and an IQR of 4. How many IQRs apart are the medians?
it.h: Divide the difference in the medians by the IQR.

it.q: Which result would make it most reasonable to say two populations are clearly different?
ch: The means differ by 3 times the MAD
The means differ by 0.2 times the MAD
it.h: A large gap compared with the spread shows a real difference.

it.q: Explain why comparing only the means of two groups can be misleading.
it.ans: If the data are very spread out, a difference in means can be small compared with the variability, so the groups overlap a lot. Comparing the difference with the MAD shows whether the difference is meaningful.

lessons.u: Module 6: Geometry
lessons.n: Unknown angle problems

it.q: Two angles are supplementary. One measures 65 degrees. What is the measure of the other angle, in degrees?
it.h: Supplementary angles add to 180 degrees.

it.q: Two angles are complementary. One measures 38 degrees. What is the other angle, in degrees?
Two vertical angles measure (3x + 10) degrees and 70 degrees. What is x?
it.h: Vertical angles are equal.

it.q: Angles A and B together form a straight line, and angle A is 4 times angle B. What is the measure of angle B?
Three adjacent angles together form a straight line. They measure 47 degrees, x degrees and 85 degrees. What is x?
Explain how to find the angle that is supplementary to a 72-degree angle, and why your method works.
it.ans: Supplementary angles together form a straight angle, which is 180 degrees. So the angle is 180 - 72 = 108 degrees.

lessons.u: Module 6: Geometry
lessons.n: Constructing and drawing triangles

it.q: Can 3 cm, 4 cm and 8 cm be the side lengths of a triangle?
ch: Yes, because 8 is the longest side
No, because all the lengths are different
it.h: The two shorter sides must add to more than the longest side.

it.q: Two angles of a triangle measure 50 and 60 degrees. What is the third angle, in degrees?
it.h: The angles of a triangle add to 180 degrees.

it.q: Which set of side lengths can form a triangle?
Which conditions determine exactly one triangle?
ch: side lengths of 5 cm, 6 cm and 7 cm
side lengths of 2 cm, 3 cm and 5 cm

it.q: A triangle's angles measure x, 2x and 3x degrees. What is the measure of the largest angle, in degrees?
Explain why knowing the three angles of a triangle does not determine a unique triangle.
it.ans: Triangles with the same three angles can be different sizes, like scaled copies, so many different triangles have those angles.

lessons.u: Module 6: Geometry
lessons.n: Slicing three-dimensional figures

it.q: A rectangular prism is sliced parallel to its base. What shape is the cross section?
it.h: A slice parallel to the base has the same shape as the base.

it.q: A cylinder is sliced perpendicular to its base, through the center of the base. What is the cross section?
A square pyramid is sliced parallel to its base. What is the cross section?
ch: a rectangle that is not a square

it.q: A cone is sliced through its top point, perpendicular to its base. What is the cross section?
A rectangular prism is 8 cm by 5 cm by 3 cm. It is sliced parallel to its 8 cm by 5 cm base. What is the area of the cross section, in square cm?
Describe two different cross sections you can make by slicing a cube, and how to make each.
it.ans: Slicing parallel to a face gives a square. Slicing off a corner, cutting the three edges that meet at that corner, gives a triangle.

lessons.u: Module 6: Geometry
lessons.n: Area, surface area and volume problems

it.q: A rectangular prism is 5 m by 4 m by 3 m. What is its volume in cubic meters?
A triangular prism has a triangular base with a base of 6 cm and a height of 4 cm. The prism is 10 cm long. What is its volume in cubic cm?
it.h: Volume = area of the base x length of the prism.

it.q: A cube has edges of 2.5 inches. What is its surface area in square inches?
A figure is a 10 ft by 6 ft rectangle with a 4 ft by 2 ft rectangle cut out of it. What is its area in square feet?
A right prism's base is a trapezoid with an area of 18 square cm. The prism is 7 cm tall. What is its volume?
Explain why the volume formula V = Bh works for any right prism.
it.ans: B is the area of the base. Stacking layers the same shape as the base, h units high, fills the prism, so the volume is the base area times the height.

lessons.u: Module 6: Geometry
lessons.n: Area of composite figures with circles and polygons

it.q: A window is a rectangle 4 feet wide and 3 feet tall with a half circle on top. The diameter of the half circle is the 4-foot width. What is the area of the window, in square feet? Use 3.14 for pi.
it.h: Add the area of the rectangle and the area of half a circle with a radius of 2 feet.

it.q: A square tile is 10 cm on each side. A circle with a diameter of 10 cm is cut out of it. What is the area of the tile that is left, in square centimeters? Use 3.14 for pi.
it.h: Subtract the area of the circle from the area of the square.

it.q: A running track is a rectangle 100 m long and 60 m wide with a half circle on each short end. Each half circle has a diameter of 60 m. Which expression gives the area inside the track, in square meters?
it.h: Two half circles together make one whole circle.

it.q: A garden is shaped like a quarter circle with a radius of 6 meters. What is its area, in square meters? Use 3.14 for pi.
it.h: Find the area of the whole circle, then take one fourth.

it.q: A rectangular rug is 8 feet by 6 feet. A round table covers a circle with a radius of 2 feet on the rug. How many square feet of the rug can still be seen? Use 3.14 for pi.
it.h: Subtract the circle's area from the rectangle's area.

it.q: Explain how to find the area of a figure made of a triangle on top of a rectangle.
it.ans: Split the figure into the triangle and the rectangle. Find the rectangle's area with length x width and the triangle's area with 1/2 x base x height, then add the two areas.

lessons.u: Module 6: Geometry
lessons.n: Writing and solving equations for angle relationships

it.q: Two angles are supplementary. One measures 3x degrees and the other measures 60 degrees. What is x?
it.h: Supplementary angles add to 180 degrees.

it.q: Two complementary angles measure (2x + 10) degrees and (x + 20) degrees. What is x?
it.h: Complementary angles add to 90 degrees.

it.q: Two lines cross. One angle measures (4x + 8) degrees and its vertical angle measures 68 degrees. Which equation finds x?
it.h: Vertical angles are equal.

it.q: Three angles together form a straight line. They measure x, 2x and 3x degrees. What is the measure of the largest angle, in degrees?
it.h: The angles that form a straight line add to 180 degrees.

it.q: Four angles fill the space around a point. They measure 120, 90, 2x and x degrees. What is x?
it.h: The angles all the way around a point add to 360 degrees.

it.q: Explain how you know that two adjacent angles that together form a right angle are complementary.
it.ans: Together they make a 90-degree angle, so their measures add to 90 degrees, which is the definition of complementary angles.

lessons.u: Module 1: Integer exponents and scientific notation
lessons.n: Exponent notation and products and quotients of powers

it.q: Which expression equals 3^2 x 3^4?
it.h: When you multiply powers with the same base, add the exponents.
Multiply -2 by itself 5 times. Is the product positive or negative?

it.q: Which expression equals 7^9 ÷ 7^3?
it.h: When you divide powers with the same base, subtract the exponents.

it.q: Which number is equal to (-3)^4?
Explain why a^3 x a^4 = a^7 by writing out the factors.
it.ans: a^3 x a^4 = (a times a times a) times (a times a times a times a). That is 7 factors of a in all, which is a^7.

lessons.u: Module 1: Integer exponents and scientific notation
lessons.n: Power of a power, zero and negative exponents

it.h: For a power of a power, multiply the exponents.
A negative exponent means a reciprocal: 5^-2 = 1 ÷ 5^2.

it.q: Which expression equals (x^4)^3?
Which expression equals 2^-3 x 2^5?
Use a quotient of powers to explain why 4^0 = 1.
it.ans: 4^3 ÷ 4^3 = 4^(3 - 3) = 4^0. Any nonzero number divided by itself is 1, so 4^0 = 1.

lessons.u: Module 1: Integer exponents and scientific notation
lessons.n: Magnitude and scientific notation

it.q: How is 0.00042 written in scientific notation?
it.h: Move the decimal point so there is exactly one nonzero digit to its left.

it.q: How is 3,600,000 written in scientific notation?
Write 7.05 x 10^4 in standard form.
Which number is greatest?
it.h: Compare the powers of 10 first.

it.q: Write 6 x 10^-3 in standard form.
Explain why 25 x 10^3 is not in scientific notation, and rewrite it correctly.
it.ans: In scientific notation the first factor must be at least 1 and less than 10. 25 x 10^3 = 2.5 x 10^4.

lessons.u: Module 1: Integer exponents and scientific notation
lessons.n: Operations with scientific notation

it.h: Multiply the first factors, then add the exponents.

it.q: What is (5 x 10^4)(4 x 10^2), in scientific notation?
it.h: 5 x 4 = 20. Rewrite 20 in scientific notation.

it.q: (6 x 10^4) + (3 x 10^3) = ? Give the answer in standard form.
it.h: Write both numbers with the same power of 10, or write both in standard form.

it.q: Light travels about 3 x 10^5 km per second. About how far does it travel in 2 x 10^2 seconds?
Explain how to find (1.2 x 10^8) ÷ (4 x 10^3) and write the answer in scientific notation.
it.ans: Divide 1.2 ÷ 4 = 0.3 and 10^8 ÷ 10^3 = 10^5, giving 0.3 x 10^5. Rewrite it as 3 x 10^4.

lessons.u: Module 1: Integer exponents and scientific notation
lessons.n: Scientific notation word problems in science and technology

it.q: A computer does 3 x 10^9 calculations each second. It runs for 2 x 10^2 seconds. The number of calculations is 6 x 10^n. What is n?
it.h: Multiply 3 x 2, then add the exponents.

it.q: A bacterium is about 2 x 10^-6 meter long and a grain of sand is about 6 x 10^-4 meter long. About how many times as long as the bacterium is the grain of sand?
it.h: Divide 6 by 2 and subtract the exponents.

it.q: A city uses 4.5 x 10^8 liters of water a day. Which is this number in standard form?
it.h: Move the decimal point 8 places to the right.

it.q: A video file is 2.4 x 10^9 bytes. A phone can store 6 x 10^10 bytes. How many of these video files can the phone hold?
it.h: Write 6 x 10^10 as 60 x 10^9.

it.q: What is the sum of 3.2 x 10^5 and 4.1 x 10^4, in scientific notation?
it.h: Rewrite 4.1 x 10^4 as 0.41 x 10^5 first.

it.q: Explain how to decide which is larger, 7 x 10^-5 or 2 x 10^-4.
it.ans: Compare the powers of ten first. 10^-4 is 10 times as large as 10^-5, so 2 x 10^-4 = 20 x 10^-5, which is larger than 7 x 10^-5.

lessons.u: Module 1: Integer exponents and scientific notation
lessons.n: Simplifying expressions with exponent rules and finding errors

it.q: Write 2^3 x 2^4 as a single power of 2. What is the exponent?
it.h: When you multiply powers with the same base, add the exponents.

it.q: What is the value of 5^6 / 5^4?
it.h: Subtract the exponents, then evaluate.

it.q: Which is equal to (x^3)^4?
it.h: A power of a power multiplies the exponents.

it.q: What is the value of 3^-2? Write it as a fraction.
it.h: A negative exponent means the reciprocal of the positive power.

it.q: Which expression is equal to 1?
it.h: Any nonzero number to the zero power is 1.

it.q: Explain why 4^3 x 4^2 = 4^5 using the meaning of exponents.
it.ans: 4^3 is 4 x 4 x 4 and 4^2 is 4 x 4. Multiplied together there are 5 factors of 4, which is 4^5.

lessons.u: Module 2: The concept of congruence
lessons.n: Translations, reflections and rotations

it.q: The point (2, 5) is translated 4 units left and 3 units down. Where is its image?
it.h: Moving left changes x; moving down changes y.

it.q: The point (3, -2) is reflected across the x-axis. What is its image?
The point (4, 1) is rotated 90 degrees counterclockwise around the origin. What is its image?
it.h: A 90-degree counterclockwise rotation around the origin sends (x, y) to (-y, x).

it.q: A segment 7 cm long is reflected across a line. How long is the image, in cm?
Which feature of a figure might change after a rotation?
Explain why a rotation is called a rigid motion.
it.ans: A rotation moves every point of a figure without stretching or shrinking it, so all lengths and angle measures stay the same.

lessons.u: Module 2: The concept of congruence
lessons.n: Sequences of rigid motions and congruence

it.q: What does it mean for two figures to be congruent?
ch: One can be moved exactly onto the other by a sequence of rigid motions
They have the same shape but may be different sizes
They are in the same position

it.q: The point (1, 2) is translated 3 units right and then reflected across the x-axis. What is the y-coordinate of the final image?
it.h: Do the transformations in order, one at a time.

it.q: Triangle ABC is congruent to triangle DEF. AB = 9 and angle B = 40 degrees. Which must be true?
The point (-3, 4) is rotated 90 degrees clockwise around the origin. What is the x-coordinate of its image?
it.h: A 90-degree clockwise rotation sends (x, y) to (y, -x).

it.q: Which sequence maps (2, 3) to (-2, -3)?
ch: a reflection across the x-axis, then a reflection across the y-axis
a reflection across the x-axis only

it.q: Describe a rigid motion that maps the triangle with vertices (1, 1), (3, 1) and (1, 4) onto the triangle with vertices (-1, 1), (-3, 1) and (-1, 4).
it.ans: Reflect across the y-axis. Each x-coordinate changes sign and each y-coordinate stays the same, which matches every vertex.

lessons.u: Module 2: The concept of congruence
lessons.n: Angle relationships with parallel lines and triangles

it.q: Parallel lines are cut by a transversal. One angle measures 65 degrees. What is the measure of its corresponding angle, in degrees?
it.h: Corresponding angles are equal when the lines are parallel.

it.q: Parallel lines are cut by a transversal. One interior angle measures 112 degrees. What is the measure of the same-side interior angle, in degrees?
it.h: Same-side interior angles are supplementary when the lines are parallel.

it.q: Two angles of a triangle measure 48 and 71 degrees. What is the measure of the exterior angle at the third vertex?
it.h: An exterior angle equals the sum of the two remote interior angles.

it.q: Alternate interior angles formed by parallel lines measure (3x + 5) and (5x - 25) degrees. What is x?
Which reason explains why the angles of every triangle add to 180 degrees?
ch: A line through one vertex parallel to the opposite side makes a straight angle from three angles equal to the triangle's angles
Every triangle has a right angle
The sides of a triangle add to 180

it.q: Explain why alternate interior angles are equal when parallel lines are cut by a transversal.
it.ans: One alternate interior angle is equal to its corresponding angle because the lines are parallel. That corresponding angle and the other alternate interior angle are vertical angles, which are equal. So the alternate interior angles are equal.

lessons.u: Module 2: The concept of congruence
lessons.n: The Pythagorean theorem

it.q: A right triangle has legs of 6 and 8. How long is the hypotenuse?
it.h: Use a^2 + b^2 = c^2.

it.q: A right triangle has a hypotenuse of 13 and one leg of 5. How long is the other leg?
it.h: Subtract the square of the leg from the square of the hypotenuse.

it.q: A 10-foot ladder leans against a wall with its base 6 feet from the wall. How many feet up the wall does it reach?
Which side lengths form a right triangle?
it.h: Check whether the squares of the two shorter sides add to the square of the longest side.

it.q: A rectangle is 9 cm by 12 cm. How long is its diagonal, in cm?
Explain how squares drawn on the sides of a right triangle with legs 3 and 4 show the Pythagorean theorem.
it.ans: The squares on the legs have areas 9 and 16, which add to 25, the area of the square on the hypotenuse. So the hypotenuse is 5, and a^2 + b^2 = c^2.

lessons.u: Module 2: The concept of congruence
lessons.n: Applying the Pythagorean theorem in two-step real-world problems

it.q: A ramp rises 5 feet over a horizontal distance of 12 feet. How long is the surface of the ramp, in feet?
it.h: The rise and the horizontal distance are the legs of a right triangle.

it.q: A kite string is 50 meters long and pulled straight. The kite is directly above a point on the ground 30 meters from the person holding the string. How high is the kite, in meters? Ignore the person's height.
it.h: The string is the hypotenuse.

it.q: A coach walks diagonally from one corner of a rectangular field 30 m wide and 40 m long to the opposite corner, then walks back along two sides. How many meters does he walk in all?
it.h: Find the diagonal first, then add the two side lengths.

it.q: A 17-foot wire runs from the top of a pole to a stake in the ground 8 feet from the base of the pole. How tall is the pole?
it.h: Which side is the hypotenuse?

it.q: An isosceles triangle has two sides of 10 cm and a base of 12 cm. What is its area, in square centimeters?
it.h: The height splits the base in half and makes two right triangles.

it.q: Explain how you can tell whether a 20-inch umbrella can lie flat in a box whose bottom is 12 inches by 16 inches.
it.ans: The longest straight segment on the bottom is the diagonal: the square root of 12^2 + 16^2 = the square root of 400 = 20 inches. The umbrella is exactly 20 inches, so it just fits along the diagonal.

lessons.u: Module 2: The concept of congruence
lessons.n: Exterior angles and angle sums in polygons

it.q: What is the sum of the interior angles of a quadrilateral, in degrees?
it.h: A diagonal splits a quadrilateral into two triangles.

it.q: What is the sum of the interior angles of a hexagon, in degrees?
it.h: Diagonals from one vertex split a hexagon into 4 triangles.

it.q: Three angles of a quadrilateral measure 80, 95 and 105 degrees. What is the fourth angle?
it.h: Subtract the known angles from the total.

it.q: An exterior angle of a triangle measures 120 degrees. The two remote interior angles are equal. What is the measure of each, in degrees?
it.h: An exterior angle equals the sum of the two remote interior angles.

it.q: All the interior angles of a regular pentagon have the same measure. What is the measure of each, in degrees?
it.h: Find the total of the angles first by splitting the pentagon into triangles.

it.q: Explain why the interior angles of any pentagon add to 540 degrees.
it.ans: Diagonals from one vertex divide a pentagon into 3 triangles. The angles of each triangle add to 180 degrees, so the pentagon's angles add to 3 x 180 = 540 degrees.

lessons.u: Module 3: Similarity
lessons.n: Dilations

it.q: The point (2, 3) is dilated from the origin by a scale factor of 4. What is its image?
it.h: Multiply each coordinate by the scale factor.

it.q: A segment 6 cm long is dilated by a scale factor of 1/3. How long is the image, in cm?
What does a dilation with a scale factor of 0.5 do to a figure?
ch: It shrinks the figure to half its size
it.h: A scale factor less than 1 makes the image smaller.

it.q: A triangle with a perimeter of 15 units is dilated by a scale factor of 2.4. What is the perimeter of the image, in units?
The point (-6, 9) is dilated from the origin by a scale factor of 2/3. What is its image?
Explain how a dilation is different from a rigid motion.
it.ans: A dilation multiplies every length by the scale factor, so the image can be larger or smaller, while angle measures stay the same. A rigid motion keeps both lengths and angles the same.

lessons.u: Module 3: Similarity
lessons.n: Similar figures

it.q: What does it mean for two figures to be similar?
ch: One can be mapped onto the other by a sequence of rigid motions and dilations
They are exactly the same size

it.q: Triangle ABC is similar to triangle DEF, and the scale factor from ABC to DEF is 3. AB = 4. What is DE?
it.h: Multiply the length by the scale factor.

it.q: A 3 by 5 rectangle is similar to a larger rectangle whose longer side is 20. What is the shorter side of the larger rectangle?
it.h: Find the scale factor using the longer sides.

it.q: Are a 4 by 6 rectangle and a 6 by 8 rectangle similar?
ch: No, because 4/6 is not equal to 6/8
Yes, because each side increased by 2
No, because their perimeters are different

it.q: Two similar triangles have corresponding sides of 6 and 15. The smaller triangle's perimeter is 20. What is the perimeter of the larger triangle?
Explain why any two squares are similar.
it.ans: Every square has four 90-degree angles, and one square can be dilated by the ratio of the side lengths and then moved to match the other square exactly.

lessons.u: Module 3: Similarity
lessons.n: Angle-angle similarity and indirect measurement

it.q: Two triangles each have angles of 40 and 75 degrees. What can you conclude?
it.h: If two pairs of angles match, the third pair must match too.

it.q: A 6-foot person casts a 4-foot shadow. At the same time, a tree casts a 22-foot shadow. How tall is the tree, in feet?
it.h: The person and the tree with their shadows form similar triangles.

it.q: Triangle ABC has angles of 50 and 60 degrees. Triangle DEF is similar to triangle ABC. What is the largest angle of triangle DEF, in degrees?
Which pair of triangles must be similar?
ch: a triangle with angles 30, 60 and 90 degrees and another with angles 90, 30 and 60 degrees
two triangles that each have one 50-degree angle
two triangles with the same perimeter

it.q: A 1.6 m tall student casts a 2 m shadow. At the same time, a flagpole casts a 15 m shadow. How tall is the flagpole, in meters?
Explain why two pairs of equal angles are enough to show two triangles are similar.
it.ans: The angles of a triangle add to 180 degrees, so if two pairs are equal, the third pair is too. A dilation can then make one triangle the same size as the other, and rigid motions place it on top, so the triangles are similar.

lessons.u: Module 3: Similarity
lessons.n: Similar triangles and the Pythagorean theorem

it.q: A right triangle has legs of 12 and 16. How long is the hypotenuse?
it.h: Use a^2 + b^2 = c^2.

it.q: Is a triangle with sides 10, 24 and 26 a right triangle?
ch: Yes, because 26 is the longest side
No, because all the sides are even

it.q: A right triangle has legs of 5 and 12. A similar triangle has a hypotenuse of 39. How long is the shorter leg of the larger triangle?
it.h: Find the hypotenuse of the first triangle, then the scale factor.

it.q: A ramp rises 9 feet over a horizontal distance of 40 feet. How long is the ramp's surface, in feet?
Drawing the altitude to the hypotenuse of a right triangle makes two smaller triangles. How are they related to the original triangle?
ch: Both are similar to the original triangle
Both are congruent to the original triangle
Neither is similar to the original triangle
Only one is similar to the original triangle

it.q: Explain how you know triangles with sides 6, 8, 10 and 9, 12, 15 are similar right triangles.
it.ans: 6^2 + 8^2 = 100 = 10^2 and 9^2 + 12^2 = 225 = 15^2, so both are right triangles. Each side of the second is 1.5 times the matching side of the first, so they are similar.

lessons.u: Module 3: Similarity
lessons.n: Sequences of dilations and rigid motions

it.q: The point (3, -2) is dilated from the origin by a scale factor of 2 and then translated 1 unit up. Where is its image?
it.h: Multiply both coordinates by 2 first, then do the translation.

it.q: A triangle has a side 9 cm long. It is dilated by a scale factor of 1/3 and then rotated 90 degrees. How long is the image of that side, in cm?
it.h: Which move changes length, and which does not?

it.q: Which sequence maps a figure onto a similar figure that is NOT congruent to it?
ch: a reflection followed by a dilation with a scale factor of 3
a rotation followed by a translation
a translation followed by a reflection
it.h: Only one kind of transformation changes size.

it.q: A 4 by 6 rectangle is reflected across the y-axis and then dilated from the origin by a scale factor of 2.5. What is the area of the image, in square units?
it.h: Find the new side lengths first.

it.q: Triangle ABC has vertices A(2, 2), B(4, 2) and C(2, 6). Triangle DEF has vertices D(-1, -1), E(-2, -1) and F(-1, -3). Which sequence maps triangle ABC onto triangle DEF?
ch: a dilation from the origin by 1/2, then a 180-degree rotation around the origin
a dilation from the origin by 2, then a reflection across the x-axis
a reflection across the y-axis only
a dilation from the origin by 1/2 only
it.h: Compare side lengths to find the scale factor, then compare positions.

it.q: Explain why a figure and its image after a dilation followed by a reflection are similar.
it.ans: The dilation keeps every angle measure and multiplies every length by the same scale factor. The reflection keeps all lengths and angles. So the image has equal angles and proportional sides, which makes it similar to the original.

lessons.u: Module 4: Linear equations
lessons.n: Solving linear equations

it.q: Solve 3(x - 2) = 2x + 4.
it.h: Distribute, then collect the x terms on one side.

it.q: Solve 0.5x + 3 = 2x - 9.

it.h: Subtract 1/3 x from both sides first.

it.q: Which equation has no solution?
How many solutions does 4(x + 2) = 4x + 8 have?
Explain how you can tell that 5x - 3 = 5x + 7 has no solution.
it.ans: Subtracting 5x from both sides gives -3 = 7, which is never true, so no value of x makes the equation true.

lessons.u: Module 4: Linear equations
lessons.n: Linear equations in two variables and their graphs

it.q: Which ordered pair is a solution of y = 2x + 3?
it.h: Substitute the x-value and check whether you get the y-value.

it.q: The point (4, k) is on the line 3x + 2y = 18. What is k?
What does the graph of all the solutions of 2x + y = 6 look like?
Student tickets cost $5 and adult tickets cost $8, and ticket sales were $120, so 5s + 8a = 120. If 10 adults attended, how many students attended?
it.h: Substitute 10 for a and solve for s.

it.q: Which equation's graph passes through (0, 4) and (2, 0)?
Explain why the equation x + y = 10 has infinitely many solutions.
it.ans: Any pair of numbers that adds to 10 is a solution, such as (3, 7), (4.5, 5.5) and (-2, 12). There are infinitely many such pairs, and together they form a line.

lessons.u: Module 4: Linear equations
lessons.n: Slope

it.q: What is the slope of the line through (1, 2) and (3, 8)?
it.h: Slope = change in y ÷ change in x.

it.q: What is the slope of the line through (-2, 5) and (4, 2)?
What is the slope of a horizontal line?
A graph of a car's trip passes through (2, 110) and (5, 275), where x is hours and y is miles. What is the car's speed in miles per hour?
Which line is steepest?
it.h: Compare the absolute values of the slopes.

it.q: Use similar triangles to explain why the slope between any two points on a line is the same.
it.ans: Slope triangles drawn between different pairs of points on the same line have the same angles, so they are similar. Their rises and runs are proportional, so rise ÷ run is the same everywhere on the line.

lessons.u: Module 4: Linear equations
lessons.n: Equations of lines

it.q: In y = -2x + 5, what is the y-intercept?
Which equation has a slope of 4 and a y-intercept of -3?
A line has a slope of 2 and passes through (3, 11). What is its y-intercept?
it.h: Substitute into y = mx + b and solve for b.

it.q: Which equation describes the line through (0, 6) and (3, 0)?
A line passes through (1, 4) and (3, 10). What is its y-intercept?
it.h: Find the slope first.

it.q: Explain why the graph of y = mx passes through the origin but the graph of y = mx + b does not when b is not 0.
it.ans: For y = mx, x = 0 gives y = 0, so (0, 0) is on the line. For y = mx + b, x = 0 gives y = b, so the line crosses the y-axis at b instead of at 0.

lessons.u: Module 4: Linear equations
lessons.n: Systems of linear equations

it.q: Which point solves both y = x + 2 and y = 2x?
it.h: Check the point in both equations.

it.q: What is the solution of the system x + y = 10 and x - y = 4?
Solve the system y = 3x and x + y = 12. What is y?
Two lines have the same slope and different y-intercepts. How many solutions does the system have?
Solve the system y = 2x - 1 and y = -x + 5. What is x?
it.h: Set the two expressions for y equal to each other.

it.q: Explain what the solution of a system of two linear equations means on a graph.
it.ans: It is the point where the two lines cross. That ordered pair makes both equations true at the same time.

lessons.u: Module 4: Linear equations
lessons.n: Multi-step equations with fraction and decimal coefficients

it.h: Multiply every term by 6 to clear the fractions.
Multiply every term by 10 to clear the decimals.

it.q: Which is a good first step to solve (x + 4)/3 = (x - 2)/2?
it.h: Find a number that both denominators divide into.
After clearing the fractions, collect the x-terms on one side.
Distribute on both sides first.

it.q: Explain why multiplying both sides of 2/3x - 1 = 1/2x by 6 does not change the solution, and solve the equation.
it.ans: Multiplying both sides of an equation by the same nonzero number keeps the sides equal, so the solution stays the same while the fractions disappear: 4x - 6 = 3x, so x = 6. Check: 2/3(6) - 1 = 3 and 1/2(6) = 3.

lessons.u: Module 4: Linear equations
lessons.n: Solving systems of equations in real-world problems

it.q: Museum passes cost $12 for members and $18 for nonmembers. A club buys 15 passes for $222. How many member passes did it buy?
it.h: Let m be the member passes, so 15 - m are nonmember passes.

it.q: The sum of two numbers is 30 and their difference is 8. What is the larger number?
it.h: Add the two equations.

it.q: A rental shop has bicycles and tricycles, 25 in all with 60 wheels. Which system fits?
it.h: A bicycle has 2 wheels and a tricycle has 3.

it.q: A rental shop has only bicycles and tricycles: 25 in all with 60 wheels. How many tricycles does it have?
it.h: Substitute b = 25 - t into the wheels equation.

it.q: Gym A costs $20 plus $5 per visit. Gym B costs $9 per visit with no fee. After how many visits do the gyms cost the same?
it.h: Set the two costs equal.

it.q: Explain how you can check that (4, 2) is the solution of the system x + y = 6 and x - y = 2.
it.ans: Substitute x = 4 and y = 2 into both equations: 4 + 2 = 6 and 4 - 2 = 2. Both equations are true, so (4, 2) is the solution.

lessons.u: Module 5: Examples of functions from geometry
lessons.n: Functions and their representations

it.q: Which relation is NOT a function?
it.h: A function gives exactly one output for each input.

it.q: A function's rule is y = 3x - 4. What is the output when the input is 6?
Which pairing is a function?
ch: input: a student's ID number; output: that student's name
input: an age in years; output: a person who is that age
input: a shoe size; output: the height of a person who wears that size
input: a letter of the alphabet; output: a word that starts with that letter

it.q: A function's rule is "multiply the input by 4, then add 1." What input gives an output of 29?
it.h: Work backward: subtract 1, then divide by 4.

it.q: A vertical line crosses a graph at two points. What does this show?
ch: The graph is not a function
The graph is a linear function

it.q: Explain why the table x: 2, 2, 5 and y: 3, 7, 9 does not represent a function.
it.ans: The input 2 is paired with two outputs, 3 and 7. A function must assign exactly one output to each input.

lessons.u: Module 5: Examples of functions from geometry
lessons.n: Linear and nonlinear functions

it.q: Which equation defines a nonlinear function?
it.h: A linear function has a constant rate of change, and its graph is a straight line.

it.q: Which table shows a linear function?
A linear function has the table x: 0, 1, 2 and y: 6, 10, 14. What is its rate of change?
Function A is y = 3x + 2. Function B has the table x: 0, 2, 4 and y: 1, 9, 17. How much greater is Function B's rate of change than Function A's?
it.h: Find the rate of change of each function first.

it.q: The area of a square is a function of its side length, A = s^2. Is this function linear?
ch: No, because the area does not change by a constant amount for each unit of side length
Yes, because the graph goes up
Yes, because it has one input
No, because squares have four sides

it.q: Explain how you can tell from a table whether a function is linear.
it.ans: When the inputs change by equal steps, a linear function's outputs also change by equal amounts. If the outputs change by different amounts for equal steps, the function is nonlinear.

lessons.u: Module 5: Examples of functions from geometry
lessons.n: Volume of cylinders

it.q: What is the volume of a cylinder with a radius of 2 cm and a height of 5 cm, in cubic cm? Use 3.14 for pi.
it.h: V = pi x r^2 x h.

it.q: A cylindrical can has a diameter of 8 cm and a height of 10 cm. What is its volume in cubic cm? Use 3.14 for pi.
it.h: Find the radius first.

it.q: A cylinder has a base area of 28.26 square inches and a height of 12 inches. What is its volume in cubic inches?
A cylinder's height is doubled and its radius stays the same. What happens to its volume?
A cylindrical tank has a radius of 3 m and a volume of 141.3 cubic meters. What is its height in meters? Use 3.14 for pi.
Explain how the volume formula for a cylinder is like the volume formula for a prism.
it.ans: Both are the area of the base times the height. A cylinder's base is a circle with area pi x r^2, so its volume is pi x r^2 x h.

lessons.u: Module 5: Examples of functions from geometry
lessons.n: Volume of cones and spheres

it.q: What is the volume of a cone with a radius of 3 cm and a height of 4 cm, in cubic cm? Use 3.14 for pi.
it.h: V = 1/3 x pi x r^2 x h.

it.q: What is the volume of a sphere with a radius of 3 m, in cubic meters? Use 3.14 for pi.
it.h: V = 4/3 x pi x r^3.

it.q: A cone and a cylinder have the same radius and the same height. How do their volumes compare?
ch: The cone's volume is 1/3 of the cylinder's
The cone's volume is 1/2 of the cylinder's
The cone's volume is 3 times the cylinder's

it.q: A cone has a diameter of 12 inches and a height of 5 inches. What is its volume in cubic inches? Use 3.14 for pi.
A ball has a radius of 6 inches. What is its volume in cubic inches? Use 3.14 for pi.
Explain how many full cones of water it takes to fill a cylinder with the same radius and height, and why.
it.ans: Three. The cone's volume is 1/3 x pi x r^2 x h, which is one third of the cylinder's volume, pi x r^2 x h.

lessons.u: Module 5: Examples of functions from geometry
lessons.n: Composite solids and volume word problems

it.q: A can is a cylinder with a radius of 3 cm and a height of 10 cm. What is its volume, in cubic cm? Use 3.14 for pi.
it.h: V = pi x r^2 x h.

it.q: A cone-shaped paper cup has a radius of 3 cm and a height of 8 cm. How much water does it hold, in cubic cm? Use 3.14 for pi.
it.h: A cone's volume is 1/3 of a cylinder with the same base and height.

it.q: A grain silo is a cylinder with a radius of 3 m and a height of 10 m, topped by a half sphere with a radius of 3 m. What is its total volume, in cubic meters? Use 3.14 for pi.
it.h: Find each part's volume and add. A half sphere is half of 4/3 x pi x r^3.

it.q: An ice cream cone has a radius of 2 in and a height of 6 in, and a half sphere of ice cream with a radius of 2 in sits on top. Which expression gives the total volume, in cubic inches?
it.h: Use the cone formula and half of the sphere formula.

it.q: A cylinder and a cone have the same radius and the same height. The cylinder holds 90 cubic inches. How many cubic inches does the cone hold?
it.h: Compare the two volume formulas.

it.q: Explain how to find the volume of material in a pipe that is a cylinder with a smaller cylinder removed from its center.
it.ans: Find the volume of the outer cylinder using the outer radius, find the volume of the hollow center using the inner radius and the same length, then subtract the inner volume from the outer volume.

lessons.u: Module 5: Examples of functions from geometry
lessons.n: Area and volume formulas as functions

it.q: The area of a square is A = s^2. What is A when s = 7?
it.h: Square the side length.

it.q: Which formula is a linear function of r?
ch: the circumference C = 2 x pi x r
the area A = pi x r^2
the volume V = 4/3 x pi x r^3
the volume V = pi x r^2 x 10
it.h: In a linear function the input appears only to the first power.

it.q: The volume of a cube is V = e^3. When the edge doubles from 2 cm to 4 cm, how many times as large does the volume become?
it.h: Find the volume for each edge length.

it.q: Which table shows the function A = s^2?
it.h: Square each input.

it.q: A cylinder has a height of 5 cm, so its volume is V = 5 x pi x r^2. Using 3.14 for pi, how many more cubic cm does it hold when r = 2 than when r = 1?
it.h: Find the volume for each radius, then subtract.

it.q: Explain why the area of a square is a function of its side length but the graph of A = s^2 is not a straight line.
it.ans: Each side length gives exactly one area, so it is a function. But the area does not grow by the same amount each time: 1, 4, 9, 16 grows by 3, 5, 7, so the rate of change is not constant and the graph curves.

lessons.u: Module 6: Linear functions
lessons.n: Modeling with linear functions

it.q: A plumber charges $40 plus $25 per hour. What is the initial value of the cost function, in dollars?
it.h: The initial value is the output when the input is 0.

it.q: Savings are modeled by y = 12x + 30, where x is weeks and y is dollars. What does 12 mean?
A candle is 20 cm tall and burns down 1.5 cm each hour. How tall is it after 6 hours, in cm?
A linear function's graph passes through (0, 8) and (4, 20). What is its rate of change?
it.h: Divide the change in y by the change in x.

it.q: A phone's battery is at 90% and drops 6% each hour. Which function gives the charge c after h hours?
A taxi fare is modeled by y = 2.5x + 4, where x is miles and y is dollars. Explain what the rate of change and the initial value mean.
it.ans: The initial value, $4, is the charge before any miles are driven. The rate of change, $2.50, is the added cost for each mile.

lessons.u: Module 6: Linear functions
lessons.n: Describing functions from graphs

it.q: A graph of a hiker's elevation rises steadily, stays flat and then falls. What does the flat part mean?
ch: The hiker's elevation is not changing
The hiker is at sea level

it.q: A graph of the water in a bathtub over time rises, stays level and then falls quickly. Which story fits?
ch: The tub fills, someone takes a bath, and then the drain is opened
The tub drains and then fills
The tub fills faster and faster
it.h: Match each part of the graph to an action.

it.q: A graph of a car's distance from home goes in straight segments from (0, 0) to (2, 120), stays flat to (3, 120), then goes to (5, 0), with hours and miles. How many miles did the car travel in all?
Which part of a distance-time graph shows the greatest speed?
A graph of a plant's height is a straight line from (0, 4) to (10, 24), where x is days and y is height in cm. How many cm does the plant grow per day?
Describe a graph of the temperature of a cup of hot cocoa left on a table for an hour.
it.ans: The graph starts high and decreases, dropping quickly at first and then more slowly, leveling off near room temperature. It is a decreasing nonlinear function.

lessons.u: Module 6: Linear functions
lessons.n: Scatter plots and lines of fit

it.q: A scatter plot shows that students who study more hours tend to score higher. What kind of association is this?
A scatter plot of car age and value shows that older cars tend to be worth less. What kind of association is this?
A line of fit for hours studied h and test score s is s = 5h + 60. What score does it predict for 6 hours of study?
Which line is the best line of fit for a scatter plot?
ch: a line close to most points, with about as many points above it as below it
a line through only the first and last points
a line above all the points
a line that always passes through the origin
it.h: A line of fit follows the overall trend of the data.

it.q: A line of fit for a plant's height y in cm after x weeks is y = 1.5x + 3. What height does it predict after 10 weeks, in cm?
Explain what an outlier is on a scatter plot.
it.ans: An outlier is a point that lies far away from the overall pattern of the other points.

lessons.u: Module 6: Linear functions
lessons.n: Patterns in two-way tables
